bubbles had stopped. weather conditions and water conditions were rough. on tuesday, march 5, 2002 the weather cleared and chevron/texaco was able to send down another diving crew. the divers $171.342.

NARRATIVE: a one ton flat bed truck with one person driving struck a cinderblock valve vault (vault box g) at a high rate of speed, knocking the roof off the top of the vault and shearing off 3 tiers of the cinderblock walls. the truck came to rest on top of the vault with a rear wheel touching a cinderblock that came to rest on top of the valve. the driver was injured and taken to the local hospital with non-life threating injuries. there was no gas leak, fire or explosion. the pipeline was isolated and depressured from 720 psi to 100 psi to allow a 17 ton crane to remove the truck from on top of the vault box. the road was blocked to prevent cars passing until after the truck was removed. once there was access to the vault and it was again verified there was no gas leak, a unocal pipeline inspector inspected the valve and piping in what was left of the vault, concluding that there was minor damage to the valve handle, but the valve was still serviceable with no requirement for replacement or repair. the coating had minor damage from the falling blocks and the piping was fit for service, no dents, gouges, or scrathes. the site was secured and the system pressure back up to normal operating pressure. plans are to repair the coating damage; the remaining block wall will be cut down to ground level and a new concrete roof installed on top so it is flush with the ground; and four 6" bollards installed at each corner of the vault and painted for high visibility.

NARRATIVE: an explosion occurred at the tank terminal facility, resulting in a fire. several oil and distillate tanks were damaged. a new low pressure tank vent system was placed into operation and produced an explosive mixture of hydrocarbon vapor/air within the dry oil tank #1, and the low pressure flare system. the low pressure suction shutdown switch had been de-activated, allowing the low pressure blower to continue to run, pulling the developing explosive fuel/air mixture through the flare system. the explosive mixture was ignited when it was vented through the low pressure flare system and reached the flare flame, where it flashed back and burned at the detonation flame arrestor outlet. after the detonation flame arrestor became compromised, the fuel/air mixture flashed back to the blower and into dry oil tank #1, resulting in the explosion and fire.

NARRATIVE: on june 6, 2002 lyons district received a one call on replacing a gas line in sec 31,30 of t 23s r 5 w of reno co, ks for kansas gas service by brb contractors inc of topeka, ks. this was on the hugoton line on the west side of the arkansas river at hutchinson, kansas. john dumond responded to the one call (ticket #204363). john dumond met john keener with brb contractors of topeka, ks. john dumond spotted all three of our lines which all ran at a depth of 63" to 66". the lines were flagged with yellow flags that have our name and phone number on them. john dumond wrote the depth division on onoek. a&l underground is a sub-contractor of brb contractors inc doing the directional bore of the arkansas river. a&l underground and brb were asked to expose our lines to the bottom of each line where we could see the drill stem and bits were well below our line. they said that they didn't want to do this because they would lose the circulation of their drilling mud. the drill stem was not seeing any loss of pressure. after they determined that it was our line, they started shutting it in. dan jaso and mike huggans were called out to help operate the gates to shut the line keep the water out of the line. we kept about 10-20 psig on the line because of the water until the line was ready to repair. brb was handling the excavating of the damaged line and pumping the water along with installation of sand points to dry the hole up enough so we could make the repair. due to pump problems, the permanent line repair wasn't completed until wednesday june 26 at 9:00 am. ronnie young and pete garcia, williams gas pipeline company welders, installed a full-encirclement.

NARRATIVE: on march 2, 2003, at 11:52 am, a leak report was called into the nrc in block hia 555. during a routine flyover, our helicopter pilot had noticed bubbling at the ocean surgace over our hios pipeline. el paso field services operates several pipelines in the area of the leak. further investigation identified the area as a location where our hia 531 lateral and our hia 557 lateral interconnect with our hia 20" pipeline. we proceeded to shut in production on the hia 557 lateral to determine if pressure on the lateral system would drop. it did not. on march 3, 2003 we proceeded to shut in all other production in the area to prevent the continuance of gas loss. this was completed by 4:00 pm. a dive vessel with an rov was made available on march 5, 2003. the dive team identified two leaks at the subsea tie in. one was a stem leak on the hios 20" check valve which we repaired and the other was a gasket leak on 20" rtj 900 series swivel flange on the hia 531 interconnect where we found that the flange had been improperly torqued. we made the necessary repairs and returned the pipelines to service on march 5, 2003 at 10:00 pm. the gas loss and the damage to material was minimal. however, the cost to make the subsea repair was $208.000.

NARRATIVE: at approximately 11:15 pm on the evening of may 20 a pipeline rupture occurred inside the sunoco marine terminal at nederland, texas. at approximately, 1:50 am may 21, 2003, confirmation was made that the rupture had occurred on the houston pipe line texoma 30" line. identification of the ruptured line was not possible earlier due to site logistics and because of several pipelines in the vicinity of the rupture site. an upstream rapid flow drop device closed and other valves on the system were manually closed. the fire burned itself out about 3 am. the rupture and fire damaged nearby electric lines and several unoccupied buildings that were part of the sunoco terminal facility. no injuries or deaths were reported. investigation as to the cause and origin of the incident is ongoing; NARRATIVE: houston pipeline was conducting pigging operations on a section of the texoma 30" gas transmission line. liquids were being removed from the system and transferred to temporary storage tanks on the right-of-way.vacuum / transport trucks were removing liquids from the tanks when a apparent malfunction on one of the trucks sparked causing a flash fire. the actual cause of the fire is still under investigation. local emergency personnel in conjunction with hpl decided to let the fire burn until it could be more easily extinguished. no injuries were reported in the fire and no deaths occurred. a volunteer fireman was treated for heat exhaustion. bell holes were excavated to examine the pipeline for possible heat effects. none were detected. no pipeline valves or other surface equipment was damaged. following extinguishment of the fire, the pigging operation was finished and the pipeline was returned to service. no gas was lost or vented due to the fire. final update...august 07, 2009 this incident occurred during a pigging operation of an intrastate pipeline. pipeline pressure was evacuated during this liquid removal process, with the exception of 50 psig of natural gas, used to push the maintenance pig. final investigation concluded that a transport truck, used to haul the condensate from this site, experienced a malfunction of a safety switch on the diesel engine, resulting in ignition of the vapors off the frac tanks. the only product loss during this incident was the liquid condensate during the fire. property damages were limited to the frac tanks and diesel trucks owned by the third party contractor. there were no additional damages to company facilities or property.

NARRATIVE: upon completion of the failure investigation, a final report will be submitted. 3-12-04 a failure analysis indicated tha the leak occurred as a result of the initiation and propagation of a crack at the apex of a dent on the id surface of the pipe. the dent, which was located on the body of the pipe at approximately the 6 o'clock position, was theorized to be caused over time by a rock situated under the pipe. the dent depth to diameter ratio was 2.5% and the maximum axial strain in the dent was approximately 22%. the crack was oriented at an angle of approximately 55 degrees with respect to the axis of the pipe and had a length of approximately 1.25 inches. it was determined that the crack initiated on the id pipe surface. the crack is not a puncture from a rock since a puncture would initiate on the od surface. the initiation of cracking was likely associated with ductile tearing, based on the high tensile strains at the dent apex on the id surface and the 45 degree angle of the crack with respect to the pipe wall. there was no evidence that the cracking was associated with any metallurgical deficiency in the pipe. the mechanical properties of the steel meet the specifications for api 5l x-65 line pipe and the microstructure is typical of this vintage and grade of pipe steel. in general, the chemistry of the steel also meets specifications.

117 feet in length, + - 1 - 2 feet in depth, and varied approximately 1 foot to 15 feet in width. it appears that there is a gap between the two ends of the pipe in the crater measuring + - 13.5 feet. on 10/7/-2, three days after hurrican lili, another side scan sonar/ sub bottom profiler survey was performed at the pipeline incident by t. baker smith & sons inc. the data captured by this survey was plotted and reviewed on 10/9/02. the interpretation of this data by the survey company project manager indicated that the water depth over the incident changed by about 2 feet to 28 feet. the + -13.5 feet gap between two ends of the pipe remained the same in the crater. it did appear that the storm did cause a significant change in the sub-sean terrain surrounding the pipeline and the crater. on 11/16/2002, the 12" pipeline was cut at the land portion on the west side of the belle pass to separate and segment the pipeline (see attached map). a 10 - NAME: GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY, LP
NARRATIVE: on tuesday december 2nd at approximately 12:15am weeks marine ( a contractor for the army corp of engineers) was dredging the atchafalaya ship channel and ruptured the 20" pipeline. the pipeline was totally severed, caught fire and burned for almost an hour. at the time of the rupture the pipeline was operating at 915 psi and had and estimated 16,451 bbls of condensate and 1,936 mcf of natural gas in the 11 mile section. the check valve that is at the eugene island block # 32 platform closed and the line was shut-in instantaneously. gulf south notified it's spill response contractor immediately to respond. by daylight when the first fly over was made with the u.s. coast guard on board their was no significant environmental damage and the coast guard required no further response. in the meantime we had already set contractors (divers, vessels and equipment) to the rupture location. on november 24th gulf south was notified by telephone from the contractor (weeks marine) of the dredge crossing the pipeline. on november 26th the pipeline was surveyed and marked by a licensed surveyor were it crossed the channel. the survey infomrmation was faxed to the dredge barge tom james and arrangements were made with weeks marine for a gulf south employee to picked up and brought to the dredge at 6:00 am on december 2nd to make the crossing. approximately 12:15 am on december 2nd the dredge struck and ruptured the pipeline. risers removed and 1,664 feet of pipe removed from shipping channel. remainer abandoned in place on may 31, 2009.

NARRATIVE: from the station event log, it appears that due to a lightning strike near the control building, the esd solenoid tripped out initiating esd. normally the esd solenoid is held energized by both the fire and gas detection systems as well as some manual push buttons. all of these things have individual annunciation attached to them and nothing was annuciated by scada. it would appear that the lightning generated a change in voltage on the esd dc voltage system causing the esd to trip. at 2:00 am, gas control notified andrew buchanon that the station had esded. when the operators arrived at the station, the blowoffs were still blowing. the blowoffs were closed when the operators determined it was safe to close them. the reason the esd blowoffs were still blowing was because gate number 55 had failed to close as it should have during a normal esd. it was determined the reason valve 55 did not close was a rusted actuator piston on the operator. the acutator was repaired and the gate returned to service.

NARRATIVE: at 11:45 pm on september 6, 2004 northerns gas control received notification that the northrup compressor station had experienced an esd. gas control had also received alarm signals from on us highway 83. the station has two natural gas compressor units and a station dehydration unit, and compresses gas received from gathering fields into the texas a-line (txm10301) upstream of the beaver compressor station. the station was flowing 27 mmcf/d at the time of the esd. the cause of the incident was a jack bolt on the outbound discharge valve cap on compressor cylinder four of unit one came loose and allowed gas to escape into the engine room. a jack bolt is a very long bolt that threads through the center of the compressor valve cap. its purpose is toe push the valve to the point that it compresses the gasket when the valve is installed, thus forming a necessary seal. the jack bolt protrudes out of the ap completely and has a lock nut that is tightened against the cap. gas leaking from the missing jack bolt was most likely ignited by debris exiting the leak and striking structural steel adjacent to the unit. the resulting explosion caused extensive damage to the building skin, doors, windows and lighter support purlins. fire damage was limited and minimal. in order to come loose the jack bolt would have had to lose preload. preload could have been lost due to gasket failure, valve failure, improper torqueing, or improper valve assembly. an august 25, 2004 compressor analysis showed no indication of improper valve assembly. there are no findings that provide an absolute determination of the cause of the failure. it may have been a combination of the factors above or it may have been a factor not yet considered.

perrytown, tx on us highway 83. the station has two natural gas compressor units and a station dehydration unit, and compresses gas received from gathering fields into the texas a-line (txm10301) upstream of the beaver compressor station. the station was flowing 27 mmcf/d at the time of the esd. the cause of the incident was a jack bolt on the outbound discharge valve cap on compressor cylinder four of unit one came loose and allowed gas to escape into the engine room. a jack bolt is a very long bolt that threads through the center of the compressor valve cap. its purpose is toe push the valve to the point that it compresses the gasket when the valve is installed, thus forming a necessary seal. the jack bolt protrudes out of the ap completely and has a lock nut that is tightened against the cap. gas leaking from the missing jack bolt was most likely ignited by debris exiting the leak and striking structural steel adjacent to the unit. the resulting explosion caused extensive damage to the building skin, doors, windows and lighter support purlins. fire damage was limited and minimal. in order to come loose the jack bolt would have had to lose preload. preload could have been lost due to gasket failure, valve failure, improper torqueing, or improper valve assembly. an august 25, 2004 compressor analysis showed no indication of improper valve assembly. there are no findings that provide an absolute determination of the cause of the failure. it may have been a combination of the factors above or it may have been a factor not yet considered.

NARRATIVE: investigation of gas odor at sayreville tap valve j-525 on 11/09/04 revealed a defect in the hot-tap nipple (20") branch on a 42" line which caused gas to escape along the outer edge of the hot tap split sleeve. in order to find the leak, leatech was sprayed around the edges of the split sleeve. small bubbles showed gas was leaking from the outer edged of the sleeve. transco coordinated with customer companies to isolate, and then draw pressure down in a 5-mile section of 42 inch main line from a line pressure of 705 psig to 190 psig. the remaining pipeline pressure was then blown to atmosphere at the 200c50 valve site blowoff valve - b-2 on 11/10/2004. the 20 inch hot tap and 42-inch piping immediately surrounding the hot tap was cut out and sent away for further analysis. a new, hydrostatically tested section of 42 inch pipeline was put into place ad non-destructively tested at the welds. the 5-mile section of 42 inch pipeline was purged of air, packed, and placed into full service on 11/12/2004. materials to perform a new 20 inch tap arrived on site 11/15/04. a new 20 inch x 42 inch hot tap connection with support saddle was installed, and the hot tap nipple was non-destructively tested. a 20 inch hot tap was performed on the new section of 42 inch truck piping, and the 20 inch pipeline was reconnected at flanges. the lateral piping was purged of air, and the meter station returned to full service on 11/17/04.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: at 2:34 pm on december 19 a kinder morgan employee contacted northern natural gas employees to report blowing gas south of the clifton compressor station. the leak area was located and the valve section was isolated and blown down. the leak was caused by a cracked girth weld. the weld opened from about the 9:00 o'clock position across the top to the 3:00 o'clock position. metallurgical analysis indicated that the girth weld was of poor quality and may have been aggravated by corrosion. northern conducted metallurgical analysis of some undamaged welds, smart pigged the entire valve section and hydrostatically tested the entire valve section prior to returning the pipeline to service. the company also reinforced welds near us highway 24. ops was updated throughout the entire process.

NAME: GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY, LP
NARRATIVE: actual cause will be determined based on metallurgical analysis. pipe sent to metallurgical laboratory november 30, 2004 and final report is expected to be delivered the week of december 21, 2004. time of incident is the time that gulf south received first indication, a rod load alarm on longview compressor station #2 units 2 and 3 which were running at the time. operator was working on unit 1 and was attempting to put into service when alarm activated. operator observed that suction pressure on index 8 at 240 psig at approximately 9:35 pm and notified gas control. gas controller dispatched first responders at 9:40 pm. the low alarm on the scada, set at 170 psig activated at 9:45pm. a review of the pressure data indicates that the actual rupture probably occurred between 8:53pm and 8:58pm. the elapsed time until area was made safe is based on the time that the production that feeds into the line was shut in and all isolating valves were closed. the nearest dwelling was approximately 2,000 feet from the rupture site. therefore, the area was actually safe once the site had been secured upon arrival by the first responders. 1-24-05 metalurgical analysis of the failed section of pipe determined that the rupture was caused by pitting corrosion on the inside of the pipe along the bottom of the pipeline, where the seam weld was located. the appearance of the corrosion indicated it was most likely due to microbiologically induced corrosion (mic) and there was no indication that the failure initiated in the weld, but the properties of the weld probably account for fracture propagation beyond the pitted area.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: a crack formed between the ball valve¿s body and one of its flanges. the crack was approximately 12 inches long as measured circumferentially. the failed valve is being sent to an independent lab for crack morphology and analysis. because the pipeline was a sole market feed, the valve could not be readily isolated. this resulted in blowing gas being managed while a stoppled bypass could be fabricated, thus resulting in costs exceeding $50k. synopsis of march 21, 2005, edison welding institute report ewi project no. 48804csp: the likely cause of failure was crack initiation from a void type casting defect. stress imparted from the connected piping contributed to subsequent crack growth. the crack propagated from the outside surface of the ball valve as evident by the increased corrosion products found across the fracture surface. microstructure likely played a role in the crack propagation too. the presence of graphite flakes within the matrix is indicative of a weaker microstructure. sem examination of the fracture surface indicated brittle-like propagation of the crack. the chemical analysis confirms that the material is a cast iron, with a carbon composition of 3 percent.

NAME: AIR PRODUCTS LP

NARRATIVE: investigation/inspection has confirmed that a stress crack had developed adjacent to a fillet weld at the location of an applied split/coupling. the magnitude of the crack was 2 1/8" in length on the circumference of the 8" x .325 wall pipe and penetrated threw the wall to the inside of the pipe. this pipe was installed on the river bottom with less than 2-'0" of cover in circa 1940. we have no history as to why this coupling was installed other than the mating pipe segments where not of the same wall thickness ie- .325 to 340. wall. it is suspected that current flow of the trinity river and possibly buoyancy due to loss of cover contributed to the stressing of this pipe as no exterior damage was found on the pipe or coupling, nor was any corrosion of any type present. 1,100 feet of this pipeline was replaced with api5l-x42, .406 wall by directional drill at a depth of 20'0" under the river bottom per requirements set forth by the corp of army engineers. the metallurigical report is attached.

NAME: CENTERPOINT ENERGY GAS TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: on january 26, at about 10:00 a field o&m technician was performing a test at the jm-24 take-off point from line jm-23. the technician operated valve #3 (v3), by placing a valve handle extension on the below ground valve. after closing the valve the technician then opened the valve and noted that the valve stem extension handle showed to be in the open position. later that day a distribution company notified the technician that line jm-24 was losing pressure. the technician returned to the jm-24 take-off and called other company employees for help. at about 1650 hours it was determined that all pressure was lost on the jm-24 line. company personnel then responsed to purge and reload the pipeline via a difference valve configuration at the jm-24 take-off point. this incident was reported to the nrc as it was deemed to be a significant event in the judgement of this operator, as it affect several town borders along the jm-24 pipeline. the suspected gate valve will be taken out of service and examined during the warmer months for a final caused determinaton. on may 27 the suspected malfunctoned gate valve was removed and diassembled. it was determined that the stem pin had sheared and was in the body of the gate valve not alllowing it to be opened. however the stem and handle would rotate which caused the operator think it was in the open position.

NAME: SOUTHERN CALIFORNIA GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on october 1, 2004 at 12" high pressure main operating at approximately 360 pounds pressure failed as a result of being struck by a ripper one or two days eariler. southern california gas was unaware of the ripper damage until the pipeline failed, opening a section longitudinally for approximately 48". the involved section of piping was isolated and blown down. repairs consisted of removing and replacing the damaged section of piping. initial estimates of gas loss and repairs did not exceed $50,000 and as a result this incident was not reported to the department of transportation or the california public utilities commission. investigation of the incident showed that the excavator was aware of the piping, and that it was properly marked. no fire, injuries, or major media resulted from this incident. on january 6, 2005, during reconciliation of incident costs, an error was discovered in the gas lost calculation. correction of this calculation resulted in the total cost related to this incident exceeding $50,000 and as a result the incident was reported immediately to department of transporation and california public utilities commission. for any further questions, contact jeff koskie at 213-244-3283.

NAME: TEXAS GAS TRANSMISSION LLC
NARRATIVE: on the evening of december 24, 2004 at 10:30 pm (cst) texas gas' gas control dept received notification from a gauger. mr. gene giles [phone no (985)232-9830], with hilcorp engineering that our texaco-dog lake (meter no 9836) facilities were on fire. this meter facility is on a small concrete platform in the louisiana marsh. hilcorp engineering operates production in the dog lake area. texas gas was receiving approximately 17 mmcf/d rate at the time of the incident. the incident was reported to the national response center by 12:30 a.m. (cst) december 25th. after the initial call from mr. giles, gas control immediately notified the youngsville-morgan city district one-call person who mobilized with three employees from the morgan city district who arrived by contracted crew boat at the area of the platform by 1:30 a.m. and found that our platform was not on fire, but piping 10- to 15- feet from the platform was. they proceeded to isolate the texas gas piping downstream of the affected facilities. hilcorp then shut in their production and there were no active meters upstream. since transco has an "inactive" riser and side valve interconnect (no 8122) on the platform, we notified their gas control dept promptly. after our pipeline was isolated, the fire continued at the same rate. our employees reported that the fire appeared to be originating from the transco pipeline area. we reported this to transco who then began mobilizing their employees who arrived onsite the morning of december 25. they isolated both their 6-inch gas pipeline and a 3-inch liquids pipeline with no impact to the flame. at approximately 10:00 a.m. december 25, as reported to us by a hilcorp engineering representative, the flame greatly intensified. texas gas believes that this greatly intensified flame indicates the rupture of our cbd 8" pipeline in the riser leaving the platform, due to the heat from the fire. at about this time, 10:00 a.m. december 25, 2004, hilcorp engineering began manually shutting-in their production lines. the fire diminished and subsided over the next 2 to 3 hours. we had no employees at the site when this event occurred as we were in the process of changing crews and refueling the boat. this informations was relayed from the hilcorp crew boat that was also monitoring the situation. texas gas believes that the initial fire was caused by the failure and ignition of a production line owned by hilcorp engineering. the heat form this initial fire caused texas gas' cbd 8" pipeline to rupture. hilcorp reimbursed texas gas for the majority of the loss. texas gas repaired the facility on project 46867.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on ded.19, a service to three aquila communities was interrupted when a branchline regulator, owned by northern natural gas, failed to operate correctly and pressures dropped to critical levels at the delivery points to the communities. aquila experienced loss of service to a portion of their customers in the communities of pine island, wanamingo and zumbrota,mn. approx 250 homes and businesses lost natural gas service in the three communities. the zumbrota area had experienced severe winter weather temperatures prior to the incident. the evening of the incident temperatures were in the single digits with wind chill below zero. the lack of pilot gas heat allowed the temperatures in the pilot gas line to drop to ambient temperatures, which were as low as 8 degrees fahrenheit. the low gas temperatures, coupled with the temperature drop through the pilot regulator, dropped the temperature of the gas to a point that matched or exceeded the dew point of the gas stream. water dropped out in the orifice of the pilot gas regulator and froze, thus impeding full operation of the regulator. northern is filing this incident report because it considers this as a significant event under 191.3. this report is being submitted late as there was an oversight in follow-up due to the fact that the incident did not meet the $50,000 dollar requirement, there were no injuries and no release of product.

NAME: QUESTAR GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: this pipe ruptured at or near the site where a corrosion pit had been repaired by filling with weld material. construction records indicate that this repair was made prior to installing the pipe in 1955. a metallurgical investigation by ewi working in conjunction with american metallurgical services concluded that "the feeder-line 18 failure origin was in a weld region near the bottom of the pipeline." the investigation found no evidence of active corrosion, fatigue cracking, hydrogen stress cracking, or stress corrosion cracking. further, the metallurgical investigation found that "the orientation of the fracture and the distinct dog-leg appearance of the removed pipeline section would suggest an external load may have contributed to the fracture." an investigation of potential external loading did find that additional third-party fill had been placed over the pipeline in the region of the fracture, and that other utilities had been installed under the pipeline in this same area. however, it could not be concluded that these factors or other factors including naturally occurring outside forces alone provided sufficient external loading to have caused this failure.

NARRATIVE: on sunday april 9, a fire was observed at delmont compressor station. the fire was confined to a single compressor unti. transite building siding was damaged, potentially releasing asbestos into the building. the fire was quarantined due to the concern of employee exposure to asbestos. an initial assessment was performed and determined the event to be an oil fire caused by a tubing leak and broken sight glass which continued to feed oil into the fire. since there appeared to be no gas release and due to the cofined nature of the fire,texas eastern determined it did not meet the definition of a reportable incident. an air monitoring contractor was brought in and verified no asbestos had been released and the quarantine was lifted on thursday april 13, allowing a more thorough investigation to proceed after the easter holiday. the investigation was completed late on tuesday, april 18 and found rod packing damage on one of the compressor cylinders which caused a small gas leak into the crankcase. the gas vented from the crankcase into the compressor building and ignited which appears to have caused the damage to the oil system. the fire shut down the compressor which vented gas from the compressor, leaving only the oil fire which caused the majority of the damage.

NARRATIVE: gas control received a call to report gas leaking near hwy 18. schriever personnel contacted individual, who reported the location as the valve setting along highway 18. personnel were dispatched from schriever to investigate. personnel discovered a gas leaking from underground and visible at the surface under the departing pig launcher. personnel isolated the valve setting header and crossover piping and blew down the gas and the leak stopped. the leak was originally judged to be non-reportable. cost estimates for the repair later revealed it did meet reportable criteria. the dot sw region director, rod seeley, was notified. no regulatory enforcement action was recommended. the leak was determined to be in a 36" header and the header was excavated in the vicinity of the leak. the leak was determined to have been caused by significant internal corrosion in the 6 o'clock position at the weld cap on the west end of the header. the header adjacent to the leak was internally inspected and all pipe with significant internal corrosion was removed by cutting pipe from the end of the header. repair was completed by welding a cap onto the cut end. the opposite end of the header was excavated and examined by x-ray and ultrasonic means to verify its integrity. the repaired header was hydrostatically tested before returning the header to service.

NARRATIVE: leak was reported on our webb county 20" pipeline on november 25, 2006. the leak was at the location of a new hot tap installation we had made on this pipeline earlier in 2006 and the leak rate was minimal. after initial review, a decision was made to take the pipeline out of service so it could be further evaluated. this action was the initial action that made the incident reportable to the railroad commission of texas. the notification to the state occured within two hours of that decision and was made on november 25, 2006 by doug menke, operations supervisor. our initial assumption was proven to be correct in that we confirmed that we had a leaking hot tap clamp. the clamp vendor travelled to the location to inject sealant in the hot tap fitting to try and stop the leak. it was confirmed at that time that the pipe was also leaking and that a repair of a leaking seal would not handle the repair. a decision was made that we would have to cut out pipe and replace the hot tap assembly and leaking pipe. this decision caused the repair cost estimate to now exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold. operations notifed compliance of this decision via an email on the morning of december 11, 2006. based on this new information notification of this being a reportable incident was made to the nrc. the fitting assembly and pipe were sent to a metallurgist for examination. the metallugical analysis reported that one of the seals on the hot tap clamp did not seat properly and over a period of time began to leak gas into the cavity between the primary and secondary seal. in time, the secondary seal failed and gas began jetting toward the body of the pipe until such time that the main 20" pipeline was cut and started to leak. the vendor reported that this was the first failure of its type on this type of hot tap clamp installation and is taking actions to improve their seal design. the pipeline was placed back into service after a tee was welded into the pipeline eliminating the need for a bolt on clamp at this tie in connection.

NARRATIVE: on january 1, 2007, at aproximately 1200, service to the town of satanta, kansas was interrupted due to the formation of a hydrate freeze in the 4-inch inlet supply line to the satanta town border station. the hydrate freeze was found to have developed downstream of the haskell county dehydration unit and upstream of the satanta tbs. the dehydration unit and the tbs are owned and operated by northern natural gas and deliver to the local distribution company, aquila, inc. aquila provides gas service to approximately 500 homes and business in satanta, which were impacted by the loss of service. at the time of the incident the state of kansas was incurring a very severe winter storm which produced low temperatures and a significant amount of ice which resulted in a buildup of ice on power lines and power poles resulting in many poles and lines breaking due to excess weight creating widespread power outages. supplemental/final report - the root cause of the service interruption to the town of satanta,ks is determined to be from a hydrate freeze in the gas line.the hydrate freeze was determined to be caused by several contributing factors. water saturated gas in combination with hydrocarbon liquids, multiple system configurations, multiple electrical power outages which shutdown the tbs heater and the bypass of the dehydration unit on 1/1/2007 generated the conditions required to form a hydrate freeze. the formation of the hydrate freeze blocked off the gas flow to the town of satanta, ks, resulting in a loss of natural gas service to the town.

NARRATIVE: on march 26, 2007 at approximately 12:28 a.m. blowing gas and dust was reported by a passerby located in section 25, t27s, range 19w in kiowa, county, kansas. it was determined by northern personnel that the gas leak was on the m670c ksm20603)pipeline. the line was removed from service and the leak area was inspected with the determination that the cause of the leak was a crack in the girth weld. analysis and repair of the pipeline is in progress. additonal information and findings from the analysis and repairs will be reported in supplemental reports. supplemental report: preliminary mile post indicated was corrected with more precise mile post. supplemental/final report: repairs were made by replacing approximately 40 feet of pipe with new 26 inch, .375, dsaw, api5l, x65 pipe and installation of a 26 inch x 36 inch plidco sleeve. a final cost of repair was calculated at $120,455. the cause of the incident was due to a lack of fusion in the root pass during construction. the lack of fusion cracked into the fill passes and eventually penetrated the cap pass to become a leak. the root cause has been determined to mostly likely be pipe bending stresses on the pipeline causing the welds to continue to crack over a long period of time. long term additional actions are being followed through with however these cost are considered to be cost associated with the long term integrity of the line and not repair costs. supplement to final report - NARRATIVE: on 7 june 2007, a michcon contractor performing reconnaissance for environmental permitting reported leakage indications approximately 200 yards west of block valve 5 along the austin-detroit a pipeline. the pipeline was isolated between adjacent block valves, and the piple line pressure was reduced from 700 to approximately 163 psig using storage field compressors. the remaining pressure was blown to atmosphere, the pipeline was de-pressurized, and repairs commenced on 8 june 2007. a seven foot segment of pipe was removed and a new segment of pre-tested 24" pipe was installed to eliminate the leak. the pipeline was purged of air, pressurized, and returned to service on 11 june 2007. the incident was reported to the national response center at 1543 hours on 8 june 2007 when it was determined that the total cost of the repair would exceed $50,000, primarily due to the volume of gas being blown to atmosphere between adjacent isolating valves. upon excavating the pipeline the leak was found on an old, previous repair consisting of a 2-inch steel coupling welded over a leaking girth weld. the coupling and plug had been installed at the 12 o'clock (top) position of the pipeline over the field girth weld and a longitudinal weld seam of the pipe. the coupling had been plugged with a two-inch threaded steel bull plug where the threads had then been sealed by welding. leakage was observed at the welded threads between the coupling and the bull plug.

NAME: CAROLINA GAS TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: when the remotely controlled inlet valve @ calpine m&r station 25-079 briefly closed as a result of a lightning strike, the station pressure was reduced from ~580 psig to ~150 psig. when the inlet valve reopened and the pressure returned, the relief didn't have time to reload to the set point (650 psig) and lifted prematurely at ~492 psig. the relief lifted so abruptly that the piston hung in the housing and would not reseat. gas control was unable to close the inlet valve to stop the relief from blowing due to the lightning damage to the communications equipment. the relief blew for approximately 66 minutes until manually valved off. maops were not exceeded.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE
NARRATIVE: a local sheriff reported to company gas control that a relief valve was discharging on tgp's 100-2 pipeline in tyler county, tx near woodville. upon arriving at the site, company personnel found that a 3/8" pipe nipple where a relief valve sensing line connected to the transmission pipeline had cracked in the threads of the nipple. this caused the sensing line to lose the "signal" to the relief valve, resulting in a discharge of gas through an 8" relief valve stack. isolation valves upstream and downstream had to be closed in order to vacate the gas from the valve section. the result was almost $300,000 in gas loss. a new nipple was installed with the relief valve sensing line reinserted. the pipeline and relief valve were placed back into service.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on august 10, 2007 northern natural gas completed nstallation of a 24-inch pigable bypass piping to facilitate removal of lateral lines to the northern natural gas compression platform mi 686 c-cmp. all work was completed and the piping was re-pressurized and leak tested. late that day personnel in aircraft witnessed bubbles on the ocean surface in the work area that were indicative of a gas leak from the piping. producer platforms were notified to shut-in and the line was isolated. this was reported to mms and the coast guard. pressure was reduced on the line. a repair plan was submitted to & approved by mms. investigation found that there was a small crack on a 2-inch bypass line that went around a 24-inch sub sea block valve. while working on repairing this leak by removing the 2 inch connection piping to the 24-inch line as well as the saddle to facilitate installation of a 24-inch leak clamp, it was found that the 2-inch connection on the other side of the block valve was also cracked. a revised repair plan was submitted and approved by mms. the revised plan called for removal of the two inch pipe and saddle identical to what was completed on the other side of the valve and installation of a high pressure, full encirclement, bolt-on leak clamp. both leak clamps were installed and a leak test at normal operating pressure was conducted for 2 hours. there were no leaks observed and the piping was wrapped and sandbagged to original cover. this was completed on august 31, 2007. the root cause of the leaks is still under investigation as it is thought that the contractor cracked the pipe when installing sandbags after the 24 inch bypass line installation was complete. a metallurgical analysis is being conducted on the 2-inch removed piping. a supplemental/final report is being filed with update to the cost of gas loss and repairs.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS COMPANY
NARRATIVE: at approximately 12:04 p.m. on september 4, 2007, northern natural gas company (nng) received notification of a possible leak in the west cameron, block 215 area. this is the 16-inch, los11202, segment 5244 line which begins in west cameron area block 222 and continues to a platform in west cameron block 192. initial reports were that there was an approximate 6 foot area of bubbles with no visible sheen. notifications were made to the nrc ticket #847779, the mms and the coast guard. immediate actions were taken to shut in production and isolate the line. a blow down and repair plan was submitted to the mms for review and approval. approval was granted. pressure on the line was reduced to approximately 35 psig. the leak area was excavated, approximately 48 inches of concrete was removed and repair of the leak accomplished by installation of a 16 inch x 18 inch plidco high pressure, full encirclement bolt on leak clamp rated at 1,500 psig. following successful installation of the leak clamp the line was brought back up to normal operating pressure and a two hour leak conducted. the pressure test was completed at 1 a.m. on september 19. following verification of no leaks for the two hour test period the line was properly wrapped and cover re-established by sandbagging. when a final cost of repairs is calculated a supplemental/final report will be submitted. supplemental report: corrected that the cause of the leak was localized pitting due to microbiological. supplemental final report: this report has been revised to reflect that calculated cost of repair. cause of the leak has been determined to be attributed to a localized pit which was due to microbiological influenced corrosion (mic). this report is closed with no further actions pending.

NAME: CONSUMERS ENERGY
NARRATIVE: the pipeline failure occurred on a 12- inch storage field line operating in a class 1 area and was in a normal operating position at the time of the failure. the pipeline was a section of the main line between the compressor station and the storage field. the line was being used as a storage field injection line operating at 1,467 psig when the incident occurred. the line ruptured, ignited and was shut in by storage field personnel by closing system valves. the system was shut in and the fire was extinguished in 27 minutes from the time of rupture. poor seam quality and corrosion were identified as the cause of the failure. seam defects, seam position, expansion and contraction assiciated with normal operating pressures, and crevice corrosion were contributing factors to the failure. the telephonic report was submitted on october 8, 2007 to mr. snowden and the report number was 851071. this report is being submitted to correct a date error in part a, item 7, telephonic report date from 2002 to 2007.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on november 3, 2007 @ approximately 8:51 a.m. the texas ochiltree county sheriff's department received a 911 call reporting a fire at northern's perryton-barlow field compressor station. northen was immediately notified an personnel were dispatched. upon arrival it was confirmed that the glycol dehydrator unit, located at the perryton-barlow compressor station was on fire. after assessing the situation, and taking into consideration the proximity of the fire to the emergency blow-down piping, it was determined that the emergency shutdown system for the station could safely be activated. the local fire department exitinguished the fire. investigation into the incident found that the fire had occurred on the dehydrator skid with most of the damage centered at the variable frequency drive (vfd) for the glycol pumps, which is believed to be the origin of the fire. it appears the fire was fueled by hydrocarbon condensate and glycol spilling out the overflow vent stack, located on the dehydrator skid, onto the vfd controls for the vfd. the positioning of the vfd as it related to the overflow vent stack was a contributing factor. additional investigation indicates that as some point the glycol recirculating pumps must have stopped working which allowed the mixture of hydrocarbon condenstate and glycol to drain back to the overflow tank resulting in a spill from the overflow piping onto the vfd controls. northern is currently working with equipment vendors to acquire cost and avilability of replacing the dehydrator unit. a current estimate of replacement is estimated at approximately $140,000. supplemental report filed to indicate/clarify part a, item g class location description is: onshore, class 1. supplemental/final report - a final cost of $152,907 has been determined to replace the damaged dehy unit and the associated electrical and control panels. this item is considered closed with no further actions planned.

NAME: CROSSTEX LIG, LLC
NARRATIVE: on october 30, 2007, at 0927 hours, crosstex lig, l.l.c. (crosstex), a subsidiary of crosstex energy services, l.p. reported a natural gas and condensate release from their 6-inch underground transmission pipeline in de soto parish, louisiana. the release was caused by a backhoe striking and damaging the pipeline during excavation. crosstex reported the unauthorized release to the louisiana emergency hazardous materials hotline (incident no. 07-06604), and the national response center (nrc) was also notified of the event (incident no. 853067). after the initial emergency response, it was determined during the investigation that the cause of the release and subsequent condensate spill was from an unidentified tap valve that was inadvertently broken off by a contractor utilizing excavation equipment during construction activities, creating an approximate 2-inch hole in the pipeline. crosstex personnel were previously unaware of the presence of such tap valve as it was not indicated on facility drawings. crosstex personnel on the scene of the incident quickly isolated the affected pipeline segment, and carefully excavated around the damaged tap valve gaining access to the damaged portion of the pipeline. repairs to the pipeline and purging activities were finalized by 1645 hours and gas service to the town of logansport was restored by 1750 hours the day of the incident. there was one injury associated with incident which occurred when the contract backhoe operator exited the excavator and twisted his knee. he was taken to a local hospital for a doctor's examination and was released the same day. however it is anticipated that additional treatment will be required due the nature of the injury. 200 mcf (thousand cubic feet)or approximately 9,341 pounds of sweet natural gas and less than two (2) barrels of condensate were released. a cleanup crew trained in emergency response was summoned by crosstex to remove soils impacted by condensate. the excavated materials were properly stored in the covered roll-off bins pending transportation to an off-site location for proper disposal. subsequent to the cleanup activities, a number of confirmatory soil samples are scheduled for collection by 11/09/07. upon receipt of the analytical data deomonstrating no presence of condensate in the affected area, clean fill will be placed over the excavated area.

NAME: CENTERPOINT ENERGY GAS TRANSMISSION
NARRATIVE: 2/27/08-5:30pm, found leak in pasture in class 1 location at station 750+43, of unknown cause on jm-30 by locating odorized gas smell. there was no sound of gas escaping or hole in the ground or visible indications of a severe leak. monitored leak through out the night by manning site with employees to provide public safety. 2/28/08 ¿ 7:30am, dispatched personnel to blockgates at each end of section and begin lowering pressure from 950 #¿s to equalize with southern section of jm-30 at 500 #¿s before digging. isolated section and began feeding southern end of jm-30 with alternate pipeline bt-14. once pressure was at 500 #¿s we began digging up location of leak to determine cause and extent of leak. when pipe was exposed we found a longitudal crack of approx. 1 inch. at that time we lowered said section down to 320#¿s by blowing gas to the atmosphere. from that time forward we began process of replacing section of pipe with crack. we continued to monitor the leak site on a 24hr shift, we manned the block valves at each end on 24 hr shift and manually fed that section to keep at 320 #¿s and maintain customers. 2/29/08 7:30am, we proccured fittings and began installing stopple fittings on each side of section of pipe leaking. continued monitoring efforts on 24 hr shift at blockgates and leak site. 3/01/08-7:30am, began utilizing stopple equipment to isolate leaking section of pipe for replacement same day. late evening hours approx 20:00 hrs we will put pipeline back in service, will update this report with actual time of inservice on supplemental report. we are sending 6 ft of leaking section with crack to: keifner and associates, inc. materials test facility, 6384 proprietors rd., worthington, ohio, 43085. phone # NAME: SOUTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: a third party noticed hole in ground and hissing sound in the vicinity of southern natural gas (sng) company's 18" south main pipeline. he reported this to sng and company personnel were dispatched to the site. upon isolation and blowdown of the valve section, the line was excavated and a crack in the circumferential weld or weld area was found to be the source of the leaking gas. metallurgical analysis revealed poorly completed welding during the original construction that failed due to tensile stresses along the pipe in a longitudinal direction. further investigation showed that the backfill surrounding the pipeline had been disturbed for construction on a parallel pipeline. the failed pipeline may not have been adequately supported before its cover was restored, resulting in the extra tensile stresses. about 80 feet of pipe was removed and replaced with new pipe. the pipeline segment is back in service.

NAME: VIKING GAS TRANSMISSION CO
CAUSE_DETAILS: CAR, TRUCK OR OTHER VEHICLE NOT RELATED TO EXCAVATION ACTIVITY
NARRATIVE: the 6" 45 degree fitting was sent to a testing lab for failure analysis. during construction of the grand forks levee by the army corps of engineers, heavy equipment may have crossed the pipeline in this location, which may have initiated the cracking of the fitting and resultant failure. the results of the analysis concluded: 1) excessive external strain caused transverse cracks in the epoxy coating and and were probably related to above ground forces directly over the pipeline elbow. 2) the cracks in the epoxy coating resulted in separation of the coating from the pipe. 3) there were numerous crack like features (clf) on the inside surface of the elbow. two fatigue cracks initated at these clf's and continued to crack through the entire wall thickness until leakage occurred. the primary cause of the failed fitting and gas leakage was external stresses.

NAME: ENTERPRISE PRODUCTS OPERATING LLC
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: gas bubbles were detected at the surface of mc 920. after investigation, it was determined that the flex joint seal ring was leaking. pipeline was secured and repair procedures have been implemented and work is ongoing. the offshore replacement operation of the 20¿ flex-joint o-ring was performed in three (3) phases: phase i, detailed inspection and initial bolt tightening april 9, to april 23, 2008 phase ii, flex-joint o-ring replacement april 24, to june 16, 2008 phase iii, final bolt tightening, ut verification, testing july 28, to august 8, 2008 enterprise confirms the 20 inch flex-joint o-ring remediation was successfully completed in accordance with the work plan, and on august 9, 2008 normal production was resumed in the gas export pipeline. for the post inspection period, august 8, to sept 8, 2008, ¿remote cameras¿ were used to monitor the flex-joint. enterprise and oil states have worked closely to analyze and evaluate both historic and project data on the flex-joint and incident to best determine the direct cause of the leak. there was no identified single item or clear direct cause for the leak. however, the evaluation and analysis points to a series of events that together most likely contributed to the cause of the leak. the factors identified included possible incorrect attach flange bolt torque value readings during the final manufacturing shop assembly, which could allow excess attach flange deflection, and slight bolt relaxation during hydrotesting. the o-ring design, dimension, and dissimilar materials were also a factor. after offshore installation of the flex-joint and during pipeline operations, fretting began to take place within the o-ring seal system. this development then led to the progression of minor corrosion, and induction of sea water, which after a period of time progressed until the leak started. during the offshore repair phases, corrective actions were implemented to address each of the potential causes, which included a newly designed larger o-ring which is now the same material as the attach flange, and accurate bolt torquing measured and verified by ut stud elongation process. this ut process eliminates any unknown friction factors which affect bolt torque values.

NAME: ATLANTA GAS LIGHT CO
NARRATIVE: this incident began as a grade 2 leak discovered at a valve box over a 6-inch valve connecting to a 24-inch main during the annual leakage survey which did not require immediate attention at the time of discoverey. however, it was discovered seven days later during repair that the leak was actually located on the 24-inch steel main above the 6-inch welded connection. for this reason, repairs to the 24-inch steel main exceeded the $50,000 requirement for reporting. an investigation determined that the support underneath the 6-inch connection subsided due to increased water levels in a low area. as a result, the 24" line failed in the base metal due to ductile overload adjacent to the welded joint.

NARRATIVE: on may 18, 2008, at approximately 5:30 p.m., northern's operations communication center (occ), received a call from dana eliker, a technician with aquila, reporting that there was a leak on northern's two-inch clatonia, ne branch line (neb42201)in a cornfield approximately 1/4 mile northwest of the town of clatonia, ne. the leak site is located in section 21, township 6n, range 5e, gage county, ne. northern personnel utilized a bottle truck at the clatonia town border station to provide gas service to the town while the branch line was shut off from the take off to the tbs to safely assess and repair the line. this line's construction includes dresser coupling, electric welds and screwed couplings. upon assessment, it was found that the threads on the pipe going into a two-inch screwed coupling had failed resulting in leaking gas. line pressure was reduced to zero and repairs were made by cutting out the failed coupling along with small pieces of the line, on each side of the coupling, and installing approximately 10 feet of new, tested two-inch, .218 wall thickness pipe. pressure was restored to 100 psig and the complete 1.26 miles of line was instrument leak detected. the pressure was then increased to normal operating pressure and the full length of the line was again instrument leak detected. upon successful loading of the line to normal pressure and no leaks discovered normal gas service was restored to the town border station of clatonia. the small pieces of pipe and the failed coupling are being sent to a laboratory for failure analysis to assist with determining the root cause of the failure. there was no fire, no injuries and no loss of service as there are no farm tap customers on the line and the clatonia town border station service was maintained with a bottle truck. this report is being filed as it is expected that repairs, including gas loss, will exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold. supplemental/final report - total final cost of repairs, including gas loss, etc is $283,192. based upon a outside services failure analysis laboratory report, the root cause of this failure is beleived to be fracturing of the pipe by cleavage (a form of brittle cracking) originating in the thread root immediately adjacent to the connection coupling. this event is considered closed with no further actions pending or planned. northern is schedulued addition precuationary equipment leak testing of other small diamter pipelines of this same vinatage and construction to enable early detection of leak should a similar condition occur on any of these facilities. added incident coordinates per request of jim bunn, phmsa.

NARRATIVE: on may 25, at approximately 0630 a.m., northern's occ received a call from the sibley county sheriff reporting that a passer-by had reported gas blowing in a field near gaylord, mn. operations personnel responded to the site and confirmed a leak on the mnb69801, 3-inch winthrop, mn branch line. line pressure at the time was approximately 800 psig. pressure was lowered to 350 psig. bottle trucks and stopple personnel were dispatched to the site. stopple fittings were welding on by approximately 10 p.m. on may 26 the bottle trucks were connected to supply gas to the town of winthrop, mn tbs # 1. the stopple was set in place and approximately 4 miles of 3-inch branch line were blown down to zero pressure. the leak site was excavated to expose the pipeline. the line was found to be dented and leaking, apparently as a result of being hit by a tiling machine. a 30 foot segment of pipe was replaced with new, tested pipe. due to the coating appearing to be disbonded and cracked a magnetic particle inspection was conducted on areas of the pipe. a four foot piece of the pipe was removed and transported to a laboratory for analysis. the repaired, damaged area was re-coated and back filled. the line was purged and pressure was restored to the line to be maintained, not to exceed 699 psig, pending return of lab analysis and finalization of investigation of the incident. an internal post incident investigation is being conducted. an nrc report was filed and this 7100 report is being filed as this is considered as a significant event and it is likely that cost of repairs will exceed the $50k reporting threshold. additional supplemental/final reports will be filed regarding lab analysis and final calculation of total cost of repair. supplemental/final report: an investigation indicates that the root cause of this event was that the landowner intalled drainage tile, without making a one call request, sometime during 2006, and in the process the pipline was struck. the coating and pipe was damaged which resulted in the gas leak. an approximate 30 feet of new, tested, coated pipe was installed to complete the repairs. laboratory analysis was completed and no other factors were found to have contributed to the leak beyond the damaged sustained during the drainage tile installation in 2006. this incident is considered closed with no further actions planned or pending. circumstances/particulars of the incident and cost have been turned over to northern's legal department for appropriate follow-up actions. 09/18/2012 added incident coordinates as per request of jim bunn, phmsa.

NARRATIVE: on june 12, 2008, northern was notified of what appeared to be a lazy flame type fire coming from the ground near the owasa, iowa branch line. personnel responded and confirmed that the fire was coming from the ground on what was the owasa, iowa 2-inch branch line (iab47201) in section 20, township 88n, range 19w, hardin county, iowa. the owasa branch line is approximately 0.932 miles long and originates from a side valve on the 6-inch iowa falls branch line. the point of fire was located at approximate mile post .49. the nrc, iub and phmsa offices were notified. the area of the leak and fire had incurred heavy rain and thunderstorms. it was determined that a bottle truck would be put in service at the owasa tbs so that the line could be taken out of service and the fire extinguished. a contractor with heavy equipment and mats was obtained to assist with repairs. dirt was bermed to enable pumping out water to allow excavation of the site. upon excavation of the site all indications were that the leak was caused by high voltage electric current discharge off the pipe wall. there was disbonded coating at the discharge point on an otherwise well coated line. the pipe wall was shiny and had not even flash rusted yet. there were no signs of corrosion or pitting and no corrosion deposits or scale. a single hole, approximately 3/8 inch in diameter was leaking the gas. all indications were that feature characteristics were consistent with high voltage discharge in a rapid event. the pit crater was smooth, no deposits, almost perfectly symmetrical and all metal surfaces appeared clean and shiny. repairs were made by installing approximately 10 feet of new tested, coated pipe. it is possible that the lightning struck at or near the tbs or take off as the black box for the phone line was also damaged by the lightning strike. this incident is not expected to reach the $50,000 threshold level for reporting, however due to the fact that there was a fire this report is being filed. a final report will be filed when all cost have been accumulated. supplemental/final report: a total cost of repairs,including gas loss, was calculated at $23,947. the root cause of the leak was determined to be caused by a lightning striking near or at the tbs/takeoff valve resulting in a high voltage electric current discharge off the pipe wall which caused an approximate 3/8 inch diameter hole in the line from which gas was leaking. repairs were completed by replacing approximately 10 feet of pipe with new two-inch, tested, coated pipe. this incident did not exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold but was reported do to the ignition of leaking gas. this event is considered closed with no further actions pending or planned. 09/18/2012 added incident coordinates as per request of jim bunn, phmsa.

NARRATIVE: during a storm, a transformer station at the magensium elektron plant which was about 100 yards from our meter station ,off of line a-102, was struck by lightning causing the secondary side of the transformer station to explode. apparently the sparks or debris fell or was blown inside the meter building and landed on the pressure controller for the regulator. this resulted in a fire from leakage around the door of the controller. as a result of the heat from the fire, the bourdon tube in the pressure controller was damaged causing the regulator to open up and then the relief valve started blowing. the fire was contained to the controller and a little surface damage to the actuator of the regulator. while this event did not meet the criteria of an incident in §191.3,paragraphs (1) or (2), it was deemed significant in the judgment of the operator because of the fire.

NAME: PRAXAIR, INC
NARRATIVE: valero refinery, texas city called at ~22:40 to report a hydrogen leak from praxair's system in the vicinity of their admin. building. follow-up communications indicated the leak involved a fire as well, which seemed to confirm the potential for a real hydrogen leak. valero refinery contacted local emergency responders (texas city pd and fd) who came to the site. five of praxair's personnel were dispatched to the site, including the pipeline manager and pipeline superintendent who was first on the scene). the praxair personnel did not see any fire, but could hear leaking gas from the vicinity of the high-pressure h2 meter station/letdown station (there are also n2 and o2 pipelines in the vicinity as well as an o2 meter station). neither the high-pressure h2 meter station, nor the letdown station were in active use at the time (in fact, the meter station was isolated downstream at the psa inside the valero refinery). the emergency responders blocked off loop 197 in front of the refinery and made preparations to put water on the station in case of an energy release as instructed by px personnel. at 00:30, all px personnel were on-site. the texas city fd was putting water on the station. a plan was formulated to send two 2-man teams to investigate and isolate the leak. multi-use analyzers and rags fastened to the end of probing bars would be used to indentify the presence of a leak and/or burning h2. the teams would unlock, open, and enter through different gates. prior to entry, 110v power was isolated from the station. the plan was communicated to praxair operations management, the pipeline control center, and personnel on-site. hwp was issued. upon entering the gate, the team entering the north gate noted that the leak was coming from a kunkle prv on the instrument (n2) gas panel. the prv was manually closed and the station was sniffed for any h2 leaks. none were found. 110v power was restored to the station. the findings were communicated to the valero refinery and the emergency responders, and the emergency was closed at 01:05. investigation into the cause of the lifting of the prv is ongoing.

NARRATIVE: on july 18, 2008, at approximately 1 a.m., a pressure drop on the beatrice a line (nem40101) mainline was noted by northern's gas control department. pressure on the line had been consistently operating in the 490 psig pressure range. this pipeline is a dresser coupled pipeline. the beatrice area had been subject to very heavy rain and thunderstorms and warnings of potential flash flooding on rivers and waterways. an all-call was issued to the beatrice region teams. based on the pressure drop steps were taken to immediately identify towns that could be adversely impacted and they were switched over to other gas source services. once this was completed steps were taken to isolate an approximate 13 miles of this line by closing block a block valves on the line at the beatrice compressor plant and block valve # 6 on the mainline. five small volume customers were identified and notified. four were domestic use farm taps and one was an irrigation setting. as there was no outside notification of a potential damage site appropriate steps were taken for two people teams to visually check the 13 mile segment of pipe for potential signs of blowing gas and/or damage.it was found that a joint of pipe approximately 25 feet long, in a waterway, had blown out of the ground. this site is located approximately 500 feet north of milepost 50.67 in section 32, township 3n, range 6e, all in gage county nebraska. the national response center and phmsa central region was notified. there was no fire, no injuries and no loss of service to any towns. northern is currently taking appropriate actions to make repairs to the line. this event was reported to the nrc and phmsa and a 7100 report is being filed as the cost of the failure, including gas loss will exceed the $50,000 reporting threshold level. a final cause for the failure is under investigation, however it is current believed that the heavy rains and flooding of the waterway resulted in erosion of supporting dirt around the pipelines dresser coupling which resulted in additional force of water flow on the dresser couplings which ultimately lead to the failure of a dresser coupling. appropriate supplemental information such as total cost of repairs and materials required to effect repairs will be reported. supplemental/final report: an investigation into the cause of the failure determined that the cause was heavy localized rain fall wash out the dirt on the banks around dresser coupling which allowed the water force to separate the pipe from a dresser coupling. approximately 269 feet of new 24 inch tested pipe was installed to complete the repair process. an updated estimate of total cost has been entered on this final report. this event is considered complete and closed with no further actions pending or planned. 09/18/2012 added incident coordinates as per requst of jim bunn, phmsa.

NAME: DOMINION PEOPLES
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: the portion of the pipeline that failed is comprised of a bare 12.75 inch diameter by 0.312-inch nominal wall thickness line pipe that contains a longitudinal seam weld. the failure occurred at a low point in the unpiggable pipeline. the pipe was installed in 1948 and has an impressed current cathodic protection (cp) system that was energized in 1961. a ten-foot section of pipe that included the ruptured joint and a portion of the adjacent upstream joint was shipped to dnv for analysis. the objectives of the failure analysis were to determine the cause of the failure and identify any contributing factors. the following is a summary of the findings: • the rupture occurred at a groove located at the longitudinal seam weld. • internal corrosion was present in the vicinity of the groove. • the morphology of the groove and associated corrosion attack is consistent with selective seam corrosion associated with electric resistance weld (erw) seams. • the weld microstructure is consistent with an electric resistance weld (erw) seam. • the results of the chemical analysis are consistent with composition specifications for api 5l grades b and c line pipe steel in place at the time of manufacture. • the results of the mechanical analysis are consistent with the specifications for api 5l grades b and c line pipe that were in place at the time of manufacture. • the charpy v-notch results indicate that the base metal and weld metal exhibited low toughness values, which is consistent with the vintage and grade of pipe. the results of the analysis indicate that the failure occurred due to internal selective seam corrosion. the synergistic effect of the selective seam corrosion, the orientation of the seam weld (5:30 o’clock orientation), and the low toughness of the base and weld metals were three of the main contributing factors to the failure. the pipeline has been replaced in it’s entirety.

NARRATIVE: while performing pipeline cleaning with a scraper pig, the pig arrived in the pig receiver. receiver isolation valves were closed. pressure in the receiver was released through manually operated ball valves (4) located in front and behind the pig. after venting gas stopped, and with vent valves in the open position, the safety interlock device was removed from the hinged closure to permite opening of the main door. with no further gas escaping fro either the valves or the pressure warning interlock device, personnel began removing the clamp which secures the main door. as the clamp was loosened, the 14" nominal diameter main door opened abruptly and with force due to unvented gas pressure trapped in the vessel behind the blocked vent valves and safety interlock. the door struck an employee in the abdomen as it swung open. the estimated pressure in section a.8.a is based in the nature of the blockage, type of debris, are of the door, and reltively minor injury to the employee.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE CO (EL PASO)
NARRATIVE: a tennessee gas pipeline employee found, through routine operations & maintenance work, indications of a gas leak evidenced by water bubbling above a pipeline at the surface of wet ground. the pipeline is tgp's 30" 800-1 line. excavation revealed what appeared to be a crack in a fillet weld where a 12" pipe tapped through a full encirclement sleeve into the 30" carrier pipe. repairs were completed around april 27, 2009 by installing a weld tee. the results from investigation confirm that the branch-to-carrier pipe fillet weld under the full encirclement saddle contained a crack extending through the weld cap and stopping just before the root bead leaving a small ligament of metal preventing through-wall penetration. based on the lab results, the crack appeared to have propagated rapidly many years ago and then remained stable for an extended period of time thereafter. minor stress appears to have caused a ductile failure in the remaining metal ligament between the old existing crack and the inadequately fused root bead which resulted in the gas leak.

NARRATIVE: on june 23, 2009, at approximately 11:54 a.m. cdt, northern's operation communication center, in omaha, ne received an emergency call reporting that there was gas blowing to atmosphere and a possible rupture of the pipeline approximately 1 1/4 miles north of the town of bessmer, michigan. personnel were immediately dispatched to the area and it was determined that a pipe rupture had occurred on the m432b (mim10101) 16-inch carlton-wakefield b line @ approximate milepost 121.26. local law enforcement evacuated approximately 15 home sites and established a 1/2 mile safe zone. the incident occurred in the se1/4 of section 3, t47n, r46w in gogebic county, michigan. line pressure at the time of the incident was approximately 923 psig. the event was immediately reported to the nrc (ticket # 909472), phmsa, michigan public safety, epa and local and state agencies. initial investigation indicated that approximately 66 feet of pipe had blown out of the ground. immediate actions were taken to isolate the segment of line and attempt to maintain as much service to customers as possible. northern's bottle trucks were brought in and placed in service for the town of bessemer and ramsay. gas service to approximately 380 homes in ramsay was lost and had to be restored by xcel energy. service to interruptible businesses in bessemer was interrupted. the pipe in the failed segment was manufactured by youngstown and installed in 1965. it is 16-inch x 0.203 and 0.250 inch wall thickness, grade x-60 electric resistance welded (erw) pipe. repairs were made by installing appropriate stopple fittings to enable replacement of approximately 219 feet of new 16-inch tested, x-60, 0.312 wall thickness pipe. the new pipe was pressure tested to a minimum test pressure of 1620 psig. a return to service plan was developed and submitted to the central region office of phmsa for review. phmsa did not identify any concerns with the plan therefore northern was authorized to re-start the carlton to marquette line at a reduced pressure as required by a corrective action order issued by the associate administrator for pipeline safety. the corrective action order requires that the pressure at the failure site and downstream of the failure site is not to exceed 80% of the operating pressure immediately prior to the failure. specifically, the pressure at the failure site is not to exceed 739 psig. this pressure restriction will remain in effect until written approval to increase the pressure or return the pipeline to its pre-failure operating pressure is obtained from the regional director, phmsa. pieces of the failed pipe have been sent to bryan lab in houston, tx for failure analysis. an additional section of pipe were sent to keifner & associates laboratory in ohio. keifner and bryan labs will assist northern with identifying the cause of the failure and the inspection techniques northern will use to identify other risks to the pipeline system. additional supplemental reports will be filed as the root cause and final, accurate cost of gas loss/repairs are determined. supplemental/final report: this report is being submitted to update the cots incurred in the repair process of this incident. in addition, the root cause has been identified as stress corrosion cracking (scc). a corrective action order (cao) was issued by phmsa, re; cpf no.3-2009-1010h. additional actions and cost are being incurred to comply with the cao, and must be completed prior to restoration of the line pressure back to it's capability prior to the rupture. these actions and cost are being addressed via quarterly reports to the director, central region of ops. as far as cost and repair actions taken to address the rupture event, per this 7100 report, there are considered complete. supplemental/final report: do to the identification of additonal cost, from employee expense and outside services, this supplemental report is being submitted to correct the previous total cost of $674,379 to $692, 449. 09/18/2012 added incident coordinates as per request of jim bunn, phmsa.
