NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on march 3, 2023 at approximately 14:52, a natural gas release occurred at the 20150013 athlon discharge 12-inch pig launcher site located 23 miles southeast of odessa, tx in midland county. while preparing to launch a cleaning pig, the operator moved all valves involved to their proper positions as per sop. the operator visually and audibly witnessed the pig trap blow down. once the pig trap was completely blown down the operator began to open the pig trap door as per sop. the operator walked away from the pig trap door to retrieve the cleaning pig from his truck and heard a hissing sound coming from the pig trap. the hissing sound was growing louder and the operator removed himself from the area to be safe. that is when the gas pressure caused the pig trap door to open causing the release of gas from the 16-inch pig trap door. at approximately 16:35, it was calculated and confirmed that the unintentional gas loss was at 3.69 mmcf, which exceeded the 3 mmcf reporting criteria and the nrc was notified at 16:49. the bettis actuator and verse valve were removed and sent for inspection and repairs. a new manual gear operator was installed and at 14:00 on 04mar the pipeline was put back into service. **june 1, 2023, it was determined that the 1-inch main line supply gas ball valve was leaking by and likely re-supplied the actuator assembly with enough pressure to actuate the valve open allowing gas to re-enter the pig launching barrel thus causing the unintentional gas release. the leaking 1-inch ball valve was replaced with a new one. this was an isolated incident and to prevent this from occurring in the future and this site, the actuators were removed and replaced with manual gear operators. the site specific pigging procedures have been updated to include areas with actuators to lock out the supply source blowdown valve in the open position in case there is a leaking valve and to prevent gas from re-entering the pig launcher barrel.

NAME: TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION, LP (SPECTRA ENERGY PARTNERS, LP)
NARRATIVE: on march 3, 2023, at approximately 8:34 p.m. et the accident storage compressor station esd'ed releasing more than 3 mmcf of natural gas. earlier that day the station lost commercial power at approximately 6:15 p.m. the accident storage compressor station is equipped with two axillary power generators. while returning to commercial power one of the units failed to switch back to commercial power isolating the gas in a unit discharge. as a result, a 10-inch rf flange gasket failed on the unit discharge piping releasing gas within the compressor building. the esd was initiated due gas reaching 40% lel with gas level reaching a peak of 75% lel within the compressor station. the gasket was replaced, and the station was returned to service on march 4, 2023.

NAME: TEXAS EASTERN TRANSMISSION, LP (SPECTRA ENERGY PARTNERS, LP)
NARRATIVE: on march 9, 2023, texas eastern transmission, l.p. (tetlp) was conducting an anomaly dig on line 14 clin-kosc vs-4, m.p. 356.89, when the crew identified indications of a leak (i.e., bubbling). a pin hole leak was confirmed with a soap solution at approximately 12:07 ct. at approximately 14:20 ct it was confirmed that repairs would likely exceed the phmsa damage/repair threshold, and the event was subsequently called into the nrc at 14:47 ct. at approximately 16:50 ct the upstream valve was closed, and the downstream compressor station (clinton) was used to pull the pressure in the line down. at 18:10 ct the downstream valve was closed, and the line was then completely blown down to make the repair. the leaking pipe was cut out and replaced and the line was returned to service on march 12, 2023, 17:20 ct. the removed section was sent to a lab for further metallurgical analysis. tetlp had assessed the line with an mfl-a tool in early 2021. the anomaly in question was reported as having a 66% depth and was issued a due date of april 30, 2023. excavation began march 8, 2023, and during the dig process the anomaly was found to be leaking. further excavation verified that a negative lead to the rectifier had come loose resulting an increased corrosion growth rate under the connection. 06/19/2023 there were no clear indications of a problem in either the rectifier readings or the test lead readings at the rectifier, and there was no additional corrosion damage in the area. the corrosion was concentrated under the loose negative ground bed lead where current was leaving the pipe and returning to the ground bed.

NARRATIVE: on 3/8/2023 williams pipeline control was notified by a landowner of a gas smell near his property in the area of a williams pipeline. technicians responded to the area and began investigating to determine the source of the smell. technicians utilized an infrared leak detection tool and confirmed a leak from the pipeline. once confirmed the pipeline was isolated using block valves and the gas was evacuated from the pipe. after gas was removed from the system and the leak was stopped, the pipeline was excavated and the source of the leak was determined to be a crack on mainline b.� in-field hardness was performed at the crack location to confirm a hard spot defect was present at the location of the crack. the hard spot measured 364 bhn x 6.5" long x 6" wide. on october 7, 2021 williams contracted rosen to inspect mainline b (mlv 180b10 to mlv 185b5) with their hard spot ili (dmg) technology to assess for the hard spot threat. there were a total of 6 hard spot anomalies reported by rosen and 4 of those 6 hard spot features were excavated/evaluated for verification. the hardness values confirmed from these 4 features ranged from 192-208 bhn, which was slightly harder than base hardness (~170-180 bhn). all 4 features were recoated per williams repair procedure. the hard spot defect that cracked (and leaked) at mp 1558.66 was not reported by rosen from their 2021 hard spot ili. re-analysis is ongoing with rosen based on the hard spot defect found. lab testing on hard spot with crack not yet completed as pipe was sent to tdw for pull testing with their hard spot ili tool to verify capabilities. we have not confirmed hydrogen stress cracking.

NAME: WBI ENERGY TRANSMISSION, INC.
NARRATIVE: a wbi employee arrived at work on the morning of march 23 and noticed gas blowing from the relief valve. the employee called another worker for assistance and called wbi gas control to report the incident. the two employees were able to get the valve to reset and stop the blowing gas. the employees found the sensing line from the valve body to the pilot was plugged with multiple ice pieces. the regulator is used to control the flow of storage gas from the storage field to the old dehydration system. because of the low field withdrawal rate, the old dehydration system was not being used. the gas in the sensing line was stagnant and ambient temperatures were below freezing, causing ice to build up in the sensing line. the station operating practice going forward will be to isolate the old dehydration system when it is not required for low field withdrawal rates. supplemental chronology: 3/22 5:38pm gas started venting. 6:55pm the reporting threshold of 3,000 mcf was met. 3/23 5:35am a wbi employee identified blowing gas when they showed up to start work that day and reported it to gas control. 6:04am station personnel stopped venting gas. 6:05am the emergency management team was notified of the relief valve venting situation. 8:27am the emergency management team determined that the amount of gas vented exceeded 3,000 mcf. 9:03am the initial report to the nrc was phoned in.

NARRATIVE: on april 12, 2023, at about 1420hrs operations technician was contacted by a guard at a neighboring road concerning a sound coming from the pearsall compressor station. the technician notified hcc of the report and headed to the station to investigate. at about 1517hrs, the technician received additional information from the guard and notified hcc who shut down the compressor. at about 1630hrs, the technician arrived at the station and confirmed the psv on unit 1 had relieved. the psv was disassembled, and condensate was found in the sensing tube and pilot, causing the psv to lift prematurely. the pilot was rebuilt using new parts, and a drain line with a liquids trap was fitted to the pilot. on april 13, at 1623hrs, after reviewing scada information, enterprise determined the relief valve discharged 4.7 mmscf of natural gas, thus, meeting the definition of an incident per 49 cfr 191.3. the trrc was notified on at 1638hrs, incident number 2822.

NAME: TARGA RESOURCES OPERATING LLC
NARRATIVE: at approximately 01:15 sandhills plant operator received an alarm that the waddell compressor station shut down due to low discharge pressure. he notified the operations manager that there was a potential rupture on the waddell discharge 12 inch pipeline due to the sharp decline in pressure. field personnel were dispatched to begin closing manual block valves on the pipeline. plant operations personnel closed the manual block valve at the sandhills plant inlet (downstream of the rupture location), at 01:40. field personnel completed closing 2 manual block valves at ponderosa compressor station (downstream of rupture location) and waddell compressor station (upstream of rupture location) at 02:00. once all the block valves were closed and pipeline isolated field personnel began ground patrols to locate the rupture. the rupture site was located at approximately 03:08 and visual confirmation was made that the line was targa's pipeline. the rupture area was monitored using 4 gas monitors and determined all product had been evacuated from line and area was safe at 03:10. there were no fires, explosions, road closures, evacuations or local emergency response because of this rupture. the incident was reported to tx rrc as a significant event due to the h2s concentration in the line and the line rupturing. the cause of the rupture was determined to be internal corrosion. this was determined by visual inspection, previous operation history and prior metallurgical testing on different sections of this pipeline. to prevent and mitigate recurrence this pipeline has been disconnected from all sources of hydrocarbons and permanently abandoned.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on april 28, 2023, at approximately 00:39 hrs. cst, lightning struck the corinth compressor station which is located in alcorn county, mississippi. the lightning strike caused damage to a small control fuse on the plc and therefore caused the activation of the esd system at 00:40 hrs. cst. tc energy was notified by the public of a potential fire after the activation of the esd system. it was later confirmed lightning ignited the gas on horsepower block 1 (hpb1) blowdown silencer. it is unclear if the original lightning strike that damaged the fuse also started the fire or if there was a second lightning strike after the esd was initiated. local ems responded to site. nrc notification was made within 1-hour of confirmation of incident. the event was reported to nrc (nrc 1 hr. report #: 1365859 and nrc 48-hr. update report#: 1365979) at 02:18 hrs. cst. operations responded to the scene and identified the fire and gas release. the source of the gas was isolated, and the fire was allowed to burn down to a minimum where the local fire department extinguished the remaining flame. operations returned the corinth compressor station to service at 15:45 hrs. cst.

NAME: ENABLE MIDSTREAM PARTNERS, LP
NARRATIVE: a possible leak/fire was discovered on 5/11/2023 at 14:03 by operations technicians conducting annual line patrols on line o-470. technicians were changing out sign markers in the o-470 row when they felt heat coming from underneath the rocks that covered pipeline in the row. technicians immediately backed away from the location. technicians went to both the upstream and downstream valve locations to begin isolating the pipeline. operations technicians notified the ops manager at 15:45, who then notified the ops director of the situation. a conference call was conducted (beginning at 16:00) to develop a plan to isolate and remediate the section of pipe with the leak. the nrc (#1367017) was notified at 16:21 on 5/11/2023. a 48hr nrc notification was placed at 12:48 on 5/14/2023. a final nrc notification was placed at 11:29 on 5/15/2023; this update was to clarify that the pipeline involved in this leak incident was a transmission pipeline. a plan was put in place to lower pressure from 728psig (the pressure at time of discovery) to 200psig, in an effort to keep any potential flame burning until the exact location of the leak could be determined. ops technicians began blowing down the pipeline at 17:34 and got the line pressure down to 600psig by 18:11 while contractors mobilized to the site. contractors utilized a trackhoe with an extended boom to pull rocks away from the leak location...as rocks were pulled away, the flame/fire was visible; as contractors were working the pipeline was brought down to 200psig. the fire was extinguished just before 24:00 on 5/11/2023. air movers were then utilized to complete the blow down. the cause of the leak was identified as external corrosion (pitting) and the fire/flame was likely ignited by a lightning strike on 5/11/2023. a 41' segment of pipe was spooled in to remediate the leak location. the pipeline was brought back in to service on 5/15/2023 at 16:30. no buildings intended for human occupancy were within 220 yards of the segment and no domestic customers were impacted by the outage.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on may 22, 2023, at 1409 hours, a pipeline technician was performing excavation standby for a road construction project when he discovered discolored soil in the area of the m500a ventura to farmington a line at milepost 98.47. he immediately retrieved his leak detection device from his truck and performed a bar hole leak detection survey. the initial indications were in the 250 to 300 parts per million range. this is a cased crossing and indications from the casing vent were approximately 21% lel. the grade 2 leak shut down the road construction activities so that a leak investigation could begin. mnops was initially notified at 1546 hours, because of the decision to close the road and shut down construction activities. the site was secured. on may 22, 2023, at 18:13, the decision was made to replace the crossing, removing the casing in the process. at this point the cost estimate would likely exceed the reporting threshold. the leak was believed to be from a cracked weld inside of the casing. the suspected weld has been sent to a lab for further analysis. a 36-inch-long pipe sample, with an acetylene girth weld located in the center, was submitted to an independent lab for analysis. lab results were received on august 3, 2023. the acetylene weld was inspected and found to be sound with no cracking. the exact leak location was not found in the sample submitted to the lab. the sample submitted had significant external corrosion pitting. the evidence of external pitting, and the severity of the pitting in some areas of the submitted sample, lead us to believe that corrosion penetrating through the pipe wall and generating a pin hole in a discarded piece of pipe caused the leak.

NARRATIVE: on 6/1/2023 at approximately 10:30 am, gulf south pipeline company llc's operations personnel were alerted by enterprise products personnel that enterprise's well 11, which is adjacent to gulf south's petal gas storage natural gas caverns pgs 10 and pgs 12a, was experiencing an increase in pressure resulting in a surface leak. gulf south was neither injecting nor withdrawing gas from wells pgs 10 or pgs 12a, and decided not to do so until the pressure on enterprise's well 11 had stabilized. on 6/2/2023 at approximately 7:10 am, gulf south and enterprise determined that the surface leak on enterprise's well contained methane and that a possible source of the methane was either cavern pgs 10 or pgs 12a communicating with enterprise's well 11 below ground, in the salt formation. because of this possibility, gulf south called the nrc. during the investigation of this event, gulf south identified that the maop of cavern pgs 10, which is 1550 psig at the surface, increased to 1564 psig without injection of gas, around the same time of this incident. gulf south pulled gas out of both caverns pgs 10 and pgs 12a over the next several days while staying in contact with enterprise and enterprise's pressure stabilized after doing so. per boardwalk's (gulf south's) well control erp, gulf south declared a level 2 well control incident on 6/2/2023 at approximately 7:00 am, downgraded the incident to a level 1 on 6/3/2023 at 8:15 am, and closed the incident on 6/7/2023 at 9:15 am. additionally, out of an abundance of caution, gulf south has performed a mechanical integrity test on cavern pgs 12a as well as multiple pressure, temperature, and density logs on both caverns. the response to question b10a of this report is shown as, "one inch depth of cover." the limitations of the reporting system prohibit entry of an accurate response. the cavern roof of pgs 10 is 2,163 feet (25,956 inches) and pgs 12a is 4,284 feet (51,408 inches) below the surface. the additionally, the maop of cavern pgs 12a is 3181 psig. the response to question e2b shows the maop established date for cavern pgs 10. additionally, the maop established date for pgs 12a is 7/22/2013. flow increase which is suspected to be the fire damaged 1-inch relief valve on the separator. station gas flow continues to bypass the dehydration area until all repairs and modifications are NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEJAS PIPELINE
NARRATIVE: during a severe thunderstorm event, at 01:55-hours local time, a nearby landowner contacted kinder morgan tejas (tejas) gas control and reported hearing the noise of a natural gas release. at 02:00-hours, tejas operations dispatched tejas employees (the employees) to investigate the landowner's report. the employees commute to the site, known as diana junction, was delayed by the inclement weather conditions and fallen trees blocking the roads. local emergency responders and citizens were clearing trees from the roads as possible. the employees reached the site at approximately 05:20-hours and safely entered the site using tejas safe approach protocol. the employees discovered straight line winds had caused a tree, located outside the site, to fall across the site fence. a branch of the fallen tree struck the 1.5-inch valve and pipe nipple located on the side of the separator sheering the nipple in the threads allowing gas to unintentionally vent to atmosphere. the separator serves the tejas hawkins lateral line, index 520-115p. by approximately 05:22-hours, the valves isolating the separator were closed. repairs of the damaged valve and pipe nipple were completed on 06/16/2023 and the separator was returned to service at 09:30-hours on the same day. in addition, the damaged fence and non-gas structures were repaired or cleared away as appropriate.

NARRATIVE: on june 15, 2023, at approximately 20:15 local time, a fire occurred at the avalon compressor station on unit #5, 14 miles south of malaga, new mexico in eddy county. operations came upon the burning compressor, esdd the station and called the local fire department to the station. a decision was made to let the fire burn itself out. at 21:00 mountain time, it was determined the repairs and damages would exceed the $123,900.00 reportable dollar criteria and the nrc and the nmprc was notified. on june 16, 2023, at approximately 15:00, unit #5 was isolated and the station was put back online by using the other compressors. the unintentional gas loss was calculated at 1.0 mcf. the cause of the fire is still under investigation. a supplemental report will be submitted once investigation is complete. **the investigation found that condensate from the compressor throw #4 inlet scrubber leaked onto the engine-compressor skid thru a partially open (two turns open) needle valve attached to the top of a liquid drain line check valve. the condensate vapors found an ignition source (engine exhaust) and ignited the condensate. to prevent this from occurring in the future, all opened-ended valves/lines on these particular systems are to be plugged. also, recommend liquid dump line check valve replacement.

NARRATIVE: at approximately 1:25 am targa gas control was notified by a 3rd party of a fire at targa's big lizard compressor station and that 911 had been called. the controller called the field operations supervisor and notified him of the potential fire and dispatched him to the location. in route to the location operations supervisor contacted additional field operators to assist in contacting gas well producers to close gas wells supplying gas to big lizard station. at approximately 2:45 am operation personnel arrived on site and confirmed one of the engine/compressors was involved in a fire. the operator began closing the manual block valves at the perimeter of the station to isolate the station. once the station was isolated, blowdowns were open to atmosphere, taking CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: on june 26, 2023, texas eastern transmission, l.p. (tetlp) was conducting an anomaly dig to install a repair sleeve on line 1 nlrk-bald vs-5 (mp 246.7). in order to install the sleeve, the existing girth weld cap needed to be ground down to accommodate the sleeve. the non-destructive examination reports did not show any indications of cracking or lack of fusion. at approximately 9:15 a.m. ct, while grinding the girth weld cap, the welder heard an unusual noise and stopped grinding. upon inspection, the welder identified a small leak on the weld and exited the excavation area. at approximately 10:50 a.m. ct, valve section 5 was isolated and emergency officials were notified. the line was then blown down from 721 to approximately 300 p.s.i.g in order keep meter stations online. an onsite crew monitored the system conditions around the clock. on june 29, 2023, the line was completely blown down and a cut out repair was completed. the line was returned to service later that day at approximately 3:15 ct. p.m. the leak was the result of grinding into existing worm hole porosity on a vintage weld (1943). the nrc was notified at approximately 12:00 p.m. when it was confirmed that repairs were likely to exceed the reporting threshold. 07/24/2023 incident date was mistakenly entered as june 23rd. date fields in part a were updated to june 26, 2023.

NAME: MIDCONTINENT EXPRESS PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: on 06/27/2023 at 12:00 pm, midcontinent express pipeline (mep) had a reportable gas release that occurred at the mep 2 compressor station when the esd system was activated and the discharge side of the esd system did not operate as designed. the esd was activated as a result of loss of ups power supply. the use of the ups power was initiated by a tripped electrical breaker that was caused by an electrically shorted air compressor. the esd block valve that is held closed by an energized solenoid, when supplied by commercial or ups power. when ups batteries were drained, the station lost control power to the station computers, plcs and unit hmis. the loss of commercial power due to tripped breaker and the loss of ups power allowed the esd valve to open causing the station to blowdown through a fully pneumatic system. when response personnel arrived they found the station discharge side gate and discharge blowdown vent valve in an open position which led to the 50,086.93 mcf release of natural gas. the esd system by design has an interlock process so that the blowdown valves will not open unless the associated station side gate valves close. this is accomplished through a series of trigger valves. the suction side of the station worked as designed during the esd. however, the discharge side experienced failures in two shafer trigger valves which allowed the blowdown vent valve to open with the discharge side gate open. the investigation found excessive corrosion/rust within the internal workings of the two shafer valves. the shafer trigger valves were replaced, the tripped breaker was reset, the shorted air compressor was removed from service until the motor was replaced, the discharge side gate and eds discharge blowdown valve were return to their normal state and the station was placed back online.

NARRATIVE: on july 10, 2023, a welder was welding a line-stop fitting on northern natural gas company's wib14801 ladysmith branch line at milepost 1.15 to accommodate a new pipeline segment tie-in. at 1100 hours, the welder began welding the "butter temper bead pass" required prior to welding the line-stop fitting to the pipeline. seven minutes later, the welder burned through the pipeline, creating a 1/16-inch hole. when the leak started, all parties exited the bell hole and stopped all ignition sources. the best location for the line stop fitting was found to be 0.150" wall thickness. this is where the burn through occurred. the incident's root cause was the welder did not follow the procedure for welding on thin-wall pipe while in-service. the welder was out of position and did not have the minimum experience northern requires to complete this challenging welding process. on july 16, 2023, at 14:50 the project was completed, and the ladysmith branch line was returned to normal service.

NARRATIVE: at approximately 8:41 a.m. eastern daylight time on july 25, 2023, cgt's line vb ruptured (the incident). the incident occurred near interstate highway 81 (i-81) in strasburg, va, and the resulting fire of the released gas caused i-81 to close in both directions for about two hours. the incident resulted in the ejection of several pieces of 26-inch pipe, which landed on the pipeline right-of-way. there were no reported injuries, fatalities, or evacuations. the line vb failure was caused by stress corrosion cracking (scc) determined by metallurgical testing completed by an independent testing facility. the root cause failure analysis (rcfa) concluded the cause of the rupture was due to near-neutral ph (nnph) scc because of the local conditions supported the initiation and growth. conditions include the operating stress, susceptible material typical for the pipe vintage, the area of coating disbondment and/or rocky outcrop shielding the pipe from corrosion protection, external corrosion serving as a crack raiser and the environmental conditions at the pipe surface promoting the development and growth pf the nnph scc (e.g. wet-dry conditions, neutral ph, bicarbonate ions).

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEXAS PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: on july 27th kmtp was currently constructing a tie in onto the permian highway pipeline. in order to tie-in the newly constructed line, kmtp elected to use a line stop to keep the gas flowing in the mainline while tying in the new line. while operators were already on site, they discovered that the gasket on the line stop had failed at 7:20 pm. an emergency response call was held at 8:00 pm, and it was determined that kmtp would report the incident out of an abundance of caution since the release volume and repair costs were unknown. it was later determined that the release volume did not exceed the 3000 mcf threshold until 8:37 pm. kmtp isolated and shut down the line at 9:15 pm and subsequently proceeded to blow down 12 miles of pipe. applicable repairs were made, and the line was back in service on july 31st at 1:00 pm. kmtp's incident investigation determined that the double position bypass bisep operation procedure's torquing safety factor was insufficient, and it lacked details regarding the application of moly lubricant to bolts and nuts prior to the torquing process. these findings were validated when additional projects were conducted with the revised procedures changes listed below and no reoccurrences were found. kmtp's investigation and these procedure improvements led kmtp to conclude that this incident was caused by an inadequate procedure. to minimize the reoccurrence of this incident, the following procedure improvements were implemented. -improved controls over bolt torquing (particularly fitting to slab valve) including: o documented procedure review o recording pump pressures & calculating torque values, including on site sign off. o moly lubricant as required and recommended under asme pcc-1-2022 o full documentation and oversight -use spiral wound gasket with inner ring on all flanged connections. -increased torque to 50% of yield in accordance with gasket parameters and pressure requirements.

NARRATIVE: on the morning of august 8, 2023, texas eastern began an anomaly dig to expose a geometry feature (buckle/dent) at the 6 o-clock position. the line in this area was very deep (>11-feet). the upstream valve was closed at 09:39 e.t. to lower the line pressure for the excavation and repair. downstream compression was used to help pull the pressure down. while excavating the anomaly, the crew identified indications of a leak at approximately 17:00 et. an operations team was then called in to investigate the suspected leak. at 19:28 et the downstream valve was closed to fully blowdown the line. at approximately 20:30 e.t. it was decided that repairs could likely exceed the phmsa reporting cost threshold. at 21:09 et the national response center was notified. the blowdown was completed on august 9, 2023, at approximately 12:30 et. the line was then excavated and the piping in area of the suspected leak was cut out and removed. an air pressure test was then performed on the cut-out segment and a small through wall feature on the weld (12 o-clock) adjacent to the geometry feature was identified. the pipe was then transported to a lab for further analysis as to the cause. 04/24/2024 supplemental updated part g - apparent cause and part j - integrity inspections the cause of the leak was tensile overloading of the pipe resulting in a 1.5-inch ductile failure at toe of the girth weld. a bending moment exerted high tensile stress near the 12:00 o'clock location and high compressive stress the 6:00 o'clock location, causing the leak at the 12:00 o'clock location and a buckle at the 6:00 o'clock location.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on august 16, 2023, nng gas control received alarms of low pressure and zero flow at multiple stations in the seminole subsystem, upstream of the kermit, tx, compressor station. the gas controllers contacted customers in the area confirming the pressure and flow deviations. nng operations communications center contacted the field operations team on-call technician to investigate the alarms. nng was notified by local authorities of blowing gas and fire near coyanosa, tx. this confirmed the incident with nng gas control. nng operations communication center initiated an all-call to the kermit, tx, field operations team to respond to the emergency. nng gas control completed shutting-in all receipt and delivery points. the field operations team closed block valve 3 which completed the isolation of the affected segment. first responders closed two roads in the process. the fire from the failure was reduced to burning residual gas within 75 minutes of the segment being isolated. based on lab results, the pipeline ruptured initially in approximately the 6 o'clock position in an area, about a foot long, of severe, mostly circular, pitting and corrosion. this pitting bears all the hallmarks of microbiologically influenced corrosion (mic), a process where one or several strains of bacteria corrode steel. the material had been corroded to approximately 0.041" wall thickness at the rupture origin, approximately 12% of the original material thickness. further examinations of the material did not locate any other failure mechanism.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on august 18, 2023, at 08:00, an explosion and fire occurred at the centerville compressor station 860 in the "a" compressor building which led to major equipment damage within the compressor building. there was a gas release and ignition on unit 10a at tgp 860. unit 10a is a clark tla-8, with (4) enbloc compressors. the #2 compressor head end unloader (heu) flange cracked in the fillet and released the gas that ignited causing a subsequent fire. at 08:16, an operations employee pulled the manual esd handle to activate the station esd system. another employee called 911. all employees and contractors working at the station safely evacuated the facility and met at the evacuation point located at the station security gate to confirm all personnel were accounted for. in an abundance of caution local emergency responders evacuated the surrounding area for a few hours. there were no off site impacts. there were no injuries or fatalities. one employee was transported to the hospital with symptoms that were not directly related to the incident. the investigation team determined that the #2 heu assembly had an inherent design flaw from the original equipment manufacturer (oem), with a contributing factor of over torqueing the heu flange during reassembly on monday, august 14, 2023 by the local mechanical crew. the incident investigation report has been provided to phmsa.

NAME: KINDER MORGAN TEXAS PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: on july 28, 2023 kinder morgan operations was made aware of audible gas leak. a kinder morgan crude and condensate (kmcc) corrosion technician was working at a shared site with index 145 mlv 759 and heard what appeared to sound like a gas leak. operations were dispatched to valve site. operations measured the leak and determined it was due to a valve stem leak. operations gathered further information and secured the site. plans were made to begin excavation on july 31, 2023 to further investigate. investigation determined a valve packing repair would not be sufficient. the valve would need to be replaced due age and inability to repack the valve stem. the style of valve is an older model walworth gate valve. the original cost estimate to replace the valve was $120,000. the pipeline index 145 serves several major power plants. due to low severity of the leak and ercot guidance, an outage to replace the valve was scheduled for september when demand would not be as high. due to unforeseen installation changes in scope of work to replace the new valve, the cost as of september 15, 2023 were forecasted to exceed $139,700. this incident and repair is now deemed phmsa reportable due to the repair cost exceeding $139,700. total unintentional gas loss of 240 mcf.

NARRATIVE: on september 19, 2023 at approximately 0800, the control center received a call from a third party about a potential leak on the 88885654 wt apollo 6008442-wa 12in (howe 12in), located 12 miles south southwest of pyote, texas. the controller notified operations and at approximately 0900 the pipeline was blocked and isolated by operations. once onsite, operations confirmed the pipeline had ruptured. approximately 5.5 mmcf of natural gas was released. at 0730 the waha gas plant had an outage thus causing the pipeline to pressure up. the cause of the rupture is still under investigation. the ruptured portion of the pipe was cut out and sent to the lab for analysis. a supplemental report will be submitted once the investigation is complete, and the results are in from the lab. october 23, 2023 at approximately 0300, the pipeline was put back into service. the conclusion of the lab report revealed that the corrosion was primarily caused by the presence of hydrogen sulfide (h2s). to prevent this from occurring in the future, coupons were installed on the pipeline, this pipeline will be put on a weekly pigging schedule and inhibitors will continue to be injected into the pipeline. an ili run will be budgeted for 2025.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on october 5, 2023 at 06:58 (est), station 267 in hopkinton, ma experienced an esd event. the initial notification was received via scada alarms. gas control personnel notified tgp operations personnel who were in route to the station for daily activities. tgp operations personnel arrived onsite at 07:11 (est). the hopkinton fire department had been notified by a third-party and arrived onsite at 07:18 (est). once tgp operations personnel arrived onsite, they observed that station 267 was venting, but the compressor station was not fully isolated from the mainline. during a station walkthrough by operations personnel, it was discovered that the compressor station side gate valves were partially open. thus gas from the mainline was venting through the station. at 7:38 (est), tgp operations personnel closed the compressor station blowoff valves to stop venting of the gas. at 3:00 (est), station 267 was confirmed to be isolated from the mainline. since this event, station 267 has remained isolated. following the internal investigation, it was determined that a power fault in the area resulted in the failure of the station plc. the plc failure activated the building protection system, triggering the esd. due to the esd command, the compressor station vent valves were opened to blow down the units. however, the compressor side gate valves failed to properly close and isolate the station. the gas loss due to this event was calculated to be 8664 mcf. in order to prevent reoccurrence, new plcs have been ordered and will be installed. additionally, all of the compressor station side gate valves have been evaluated to ensure correct functionality. as an added precaution, operations has developed a procedure for isolating the station from the mainline during extended periods when the station is not in demand. the action items above are intended to reduce the potential for reoccurrence of this event.

NARRATIVE: while tracking an inline inspection tool on 10/25/2023, gulf south personnel identified a leak on its index 129 pipeline. gulf south isolated approximately 13 miles of pipeline and utilized flares to blow down the pipeline in order to make repairs. a 16' piece of replacement pipe was installed on 10/28/2023 and the pipeline was returned to normal service that evening. the incident cause is currently under investingation and a supplemental report will be submitted when the cause has been determined. 3/7/2024 updated parts g and j and submitted final report. the root cause investigation revealed the following: the installed reinforcement saddle (installation date unknown) was not properly fitted and was attached with an insufficient single-pass fillet weld to both the pipeline and to the central branch pipe. these welds are not sufficient to properly attach this reinforcement saddle. movement of the branch with all attached flanges, valve, and piping caused a ductile overload failure of the pipe wall that initiated at the toe of the reinforcing saddle to pipeline weld and proceeded through-wall in two or more steps. no evidence of fatigue was observed.

NARRATIVE: on november 8, 2023, at approximately 12:11 hours consumers energy gas control received an alarm notification which indicated a possible fire at the st. clair compressor station (plant 4 dehydration system building). the consumers energy st. clair compressor station is in ira, michigan (st. clair county). a station mechanic at the site was notified and confirmed activation of the plant fire-gate system occurred due to the fire detection alarm. following the event, the plant was removed from service and the scene was made safe. additional personnel were dispatched to the station to determine the potential cause of the activation. during the incident investigation, no notable indications of failures were present in the facility, but upon arrival, it was noted that a gap in the insulation on the reboiler exhaust stack was clearly visible and was presumed to be the source of a false trip indication to the fire-eye (in direct line of sight) due to the infrared irradiation from the pipe (operating as normal up to 1500 degree f). the insulation on the exhaust system was inspected with no notable issues observed, repaired, and returned to service on november 9, 2023. on november 10, 2023, at approximately 11:17 hours, less than 24 hours after the return to service consumers energy gas control received an alarm notification which indicated a possible fire at the st. clair compressor station (plant 4 dehydration system building). the equipment was taken off-line, and all insulation was removed to permit physical inspection. several cracked welds were identified on the exhaust line of the thermal oxidizer, super heater, and condensate collection system of the thermal oxidizer. loose bolts were found in the flanged connections of the system, and an exhaust pipe slip joint connection to the exhaust stack was found to no longer be inserted into the fitting. both events were reported to mpsc as required when an emergency shutdown system is activated, and gas released. however, a more in-depth visual inspection confirmed additional equipment damage anticipated to exceed phmsa reporting criteria of $139,700. additional investigations after the event have identified a concern relative to insufficient bolt torque specifications used during a 2020 repair to the system, pipe fabrication failure resulting in pre-stress being applied to the failed system connection points, and potential pinned pipe in a high thermal growth area of the system exacerbating stresses imparted to those same connection points. further problem solving is required to determine the root cause of the failure. however, with the concerns defined, consumers energy has taken action to remediate each concern through a refabrication of the super heater vessel failed components, pipe assemblies found to be creating the pre-stress scenario, slip joint insertion was increased to avoid risk of the joint failing, application of torque specifications from the original equipment manufacturer, and implementation of a preventative maintenance schedule for re-validating torque on bolted connections following return to service. further analysis is required to support confirmation of the pipe failure modes identified in the field and is presently underway. the original equipment manufacturer has been engaged in the review and repair plan and is supporting review of the stress analysis. engineering support has been contracted to support model development of the system and execute a pipe stress analysis. following the outcome of the modeling and validation of the failure modes, additional steps may be necessary to improve the integrity of the system and will be implemented accordingly. further analysis confirmed the failure was a result of insufficient bolt torque specifications provided by the manufacturer during a previous repair to the system. the failure was a result of the bolts yielding and torque was lost through the thermal cycle causing bolts to loosen.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on january 17, 2024, at approximately 06:20 hrs. cst, tc energy was notified by the public of a potential gas release at the corinth compressor station. tc energy operations personnel arrived at the corinth compressor station, located in alcorn county, mississippi, and discovered natural gas being released to atmosphere. the unintentional gas release was confirmed by tc energy operations at approximately 07:16 hrs. cst. it was later confirmed that the blowdown valve's (5sh-2d bd) stratix switch, which communicates the valve status to the programmable logic controller (plc), had malfunctioned. this loss of communication caused the blowdown valve to lose its hold closed command from the plc. the valve traveled open due to the loss of signal when the switch failed. the malfunctioning switch also caused no alarm to be conveyed to the emergency shutdown device (esd) plc and therefore, is the reason gas controller did not receive a "call out" alarm from the scada system. tc energy operations manually closed the blowdown valve at 08:05 hrs. cst. the stratix switch was replaced and the esd system was placed back into normal service at approximately 12:30 hrs. cst. the corinth compressor station was not shut down due to this incident.

NAME: WBI ENERGY TRANSMISSION, INC.
NARRATIVE: wbi energy received a call from a concerned citizen at 4:41 pm on 1/7/24 that there was a loud gas blowing sound at the golva compressor station. a wbi operator arrived on site at 5:14 pm and assessed the situation. they found the supply line tubing from the pilot that holds the relief valve closed had failed which caused the relief valve to open and vent gas to the atmosphere. the operator was able to partially isolate the station and replace the broken supply line tubing. the station was returned to normal service at 6:34 pm. the volume of gas released to atmosphere was not calculated on the day of the incident. a similar incident happened at the golva compressor station on 1/23/24 and when scada data was being reviewed, the volume released on 1/7/24 was identified and calculated. after the volume was calculated and identified as being over the 3,000 mcf threshold, the incident was telephoned to the nrc. wbi performed an investigation of the supply line tubing failure that occurred on 1/7/24 and 1/23/24. wbi's vibration technician took vibration intensity readings on the relief valve and associated tubing and found amplitudes exceeding allowable limits. wbi replaced the supply line tubing with heavier wall tubing and has developed a plan for installing diagonal supports to the relief valve and associated piping. the installation of the additional supports is currently being planned and tentatively scheduled for the first week in march. after the installation of the supports, additional vibration analysis will be performed to confirm the vibration has been dampened to an allowable magnitude. update - installation of additional supports were added to unit #1 on 2/28 and to unit #2 on 2/29.

NAME: GREAT LAKES GAS TRANSMISSION LIMITED PARTNERSHIP
NARRATIVE: on january 12, 2024, severe weather including heavy winds and snow passed through the gaylord, michigan area. when the power failure alarm was detected at 7:23 pm. est, the monitoring center called the technician on site to investigate the alarm. the technician could audibly hear blowing gas at 7:47 p.m. est and discovered natural gas was being released through the unit 1101 blowdown stack. immediate action was taken by verifying no fire existed, a second technician was dispatched and assisted in safely isolating the gas source by closing the unit valve which ended the release at 8:15 p.m. est. unintentional gas loss was calculated to 3.61 million cubic feet (mmcf). no property damage, injuries or mandatory evacuations were needed. the cause of the unintentional release was attributed to loss of commercial power at the station. the backup generator did not start, and the vent valve opened due to the loss of control air pressure. the vent valve is designed to fail open in the case of low control air and the suction and discharge valves remained in their current open operating state. no overpressure occurred. after further investigation of the auxiliary power unit (apu), it was found two loose primary ignition wires caused the engine to backfire which resulted in a small tear in the left bank secondary fuel regulator diaphragm. a low horsepower condition ensued. apu was repaired and placed back in service on january 19, 2024. modified sections a5, g2 and g6 per phmsa's request.

NARRATIVE: on 01/18/24, midwestern gas transmission paris compressor station personnel were performing a routine inspection of the station yard piping when they observed damage to the valve actuator on mainline valve 2113. as they approached the area, they noticed the mainline valve actuator had dislodged striking the mainline valve 2113 bypass line. the paris station was not running at the time of the incident. operations confirmed that the damage did not cause a release. an investigation found that water entered the inside of the stem extension housing. below zero temperatures caused this water to freeze and block the stem extension vent. during the response operations found a small stem leak on mainline valve 2113. the stem was leaking into the valve extension housing. the frozen vent did not allow the pressure to evacuate the stem extension housing which caused pressure to build and dislodge the valve stem extension. when the valve stem dislodged, it damaged the valve actuator and bypass line. property damage costs to the valve actuator and bypass line exceeded the reporting threshold.

NARRATIVE: operations management received initial notification of this incident via a call from another operator on 1/25/24 at approximately 18:06 reporting that there was a fire at big isaac compressor station (cs) (ga-1081). gas control received secondary notification of this incident from 911 at approximately 18:10 reporting that a fire department was in the process of responding to big isaac cs. at this point in time, the extent and severity of the fire at big isaac cs was not known. big isaac cs receives natural gas from h-21912 (production pipeline owned and operated by hope gas), compresses it using a single engine unit (ajax model #dpc-360le installed in 1999 with 360 hp), and discharges it into tl-413 (gathering pipeline owned and operated by egts with a maop of 500 psig). gas control notified operations management of the situation at approximately 18:15. operations management dispatched personnel to big isaac cs at approximately 18:20. gas control lost communications with big isaac cs at approximately 17:19. operations personnel arrived at big isaac cs at approximately 19:24, assessed the situation, began utilizing fire extinguishers to extinguish the fire on the engine unit, and implemented a plan to safely isolate the fire. operations personnel manually closed valve 1081-a at approximately 19:26. valve 1081-a is located where the discharge of big isaac cs connects to tl-413 which is downstream of the fire. operations personnel manually closed valve 1081-b at approximately 19:27. valve 1081-b is located where the suction of big isaac cs connects to h-21912 which is upstream of the fire. the closure of valves 1081-a and 1081-b completed the isolation of the fire. the fire was extinguished at approximately 19:36. the responding fire department departed the facility at approximately 20:20. the responding operations personnel secured the facility and departed the facility at approximately 23:20. no evacuations were necessary, no injuries were sustained, and there were no environmental impacts as a result of the incident. based on review of the scada discharge pressure and flow histories, it is believed that the fire on the engine unit initially ignited at approximately 17:19 at which point in time big isaac cs was in normal operation with a discharge pressure of 197 psig and a discharge flow rate of 832 mscfd. upon examination of the engine unit following the incident, it is believed that the fire initiated in the low stage distance piece and was sustained by the flow of natural gas. the crosshead pin and bushing seized causing increased friction on the slide assembly. the additional friction increased the temperature on the components to the flashpoint of the oil (459 deg f). the crosshead running position was altered by melting babbitt causing the compressor piston rod to rub the pressure and wiper packing cases. excessive rubbing of the compressor piston rod generated excessive heat inside a gaseous environment which allowed combustion to occur. the internal fire melted the plexiglass cover on the crosshead distance piece housing which allowed additional oxygen to enter the distance piece and sustained the combustion. the resulting damage to the engine unit and the associated frame, skid, protective structure, control panel, compressor bottle, fuel line valve, and conduit was extensive. initial telephonic notification was made to the national response center on 1/25/24 at 19:28. the national response center assigned incident report #1389962 to the initial notification of the incident. a follow up telephonic notification was made to the national response center on 1/27/24 at 09:04 to confirm the initial telephonic notification. the national response center assigned incident report #1389962 to the follow up telephonic notification. the decision was made to abandon big isaac cs as an engine unit at law cs is capable of moving the natural gas that was moved by the engine unit at big isaac cs.

NARRATIVE: kinder morgan tejas gas control received a call from a homeowner of a potential natural gas leak. km operations personnel responded and verified the presence of gas aboveground on its 202-600 line. notifications were made to the national response center and the txrrc. operations were dispatched to the upstream and downstream valves and local emergency responders (houston fire department) were contacted and dispatched. upstream and downstream valves were closed in order that the pipeline segment could be isolated, and the pipeline blown down. the leak site was excavated, and evaluation and repair of the leak began. during evaluation the cause of the leak was determined to be from a crack at a tap weld (tap had previously been abandoned). the repair of the leak consisted of the segment of pipe containing the abandoned tap being cut out and replaced with a piece of straight pipe. the kinder morgan metallurgy department is currently in the process of completing a failure analysis of the failed tap connection. upon the completion of the failure analysis investigation this report will be updated and finalized. on may 9, 2024; kinder morgan's metallurgical engineer completed the failure analysis of the tap connection. the final conclusions as to the cause of the failure were: 1) the leak was located at the toe of the fillet weld attaching a localized saddle to the nps 20 pipe; 2) the hot tap connection did not have a full encirclement saddle, and 3) the fracture was a ductile overload caused by a downward bending moment on the nps 2 branch. please note that current kinder morgan engineering standard e1100 would not permit new construction with this nps 2 on nps 20 hot tap configuration with only a localized saddle and no full encirclement sleeve.

NARRATIVE: on november 25th, 2023, at 10:45 a.m. et, saltville gas storage company, llc ("saltville gas" or the "company") received a call from a landowner reporting a hissing sound emanating from his private water well. this was the earliest indication that saltville gas had of a gas release potentially related to its storage field, which is why it is identified as the incident date/time in a4 and the date/time that a "failure" was identified in a13 of this report. the company's investigation is ongoing, however, and it has not yet identified an equipment or other failure as a contributing factor to this event. saltville gas took prompt action to investigate the november 25, 2023, notification from the landowner, as well as the landowner's november 26, 2023, report of intermittent bubbling at cove creek. the company did not confirm that the storage field was likely the source of the gas until january 30, 2024, the date an incident was reported to the national response center (nrc) in accordance with phmsa reporting criteria. on november 26, 2023, operations personnel began an early withdrawal from the underground storage field to reduce the pressure in the field, a day earlier than withdrawal had previously been planned. in the succeeding weeks, saltville gas closely monitored field pressure and any evidence of gas at the landowner's property, and it gathered and analyzed gas samples from the landowner's water well to confirm the release source. on january 30th, 2024, a gas sample analysis report confirmed that the gas discovered in the landowner's water well likely originated from the storage field. at that time, saltville gas deemed the event significant within the meaning of the phmsa "incident" definition (see 49 cfr 191.3(3)) even though it did not meet the other incident criteria under 49 cfr 191.3(1) or (2). therefore, on january 30th, 2024, at 9:59 a.m. et, saltville storage notified nrc. supplemental 07/16/2025 on april 22, 2024, saltville gas conducted nitrogen pressure tests on storage wells eh-87, eh-90 and eh-93. results from these tests were not available in time to be included in the initial 30-day incident report submitted on february 28th. both wells eh-87 and eh-90 were able to maintain pressure for the duration of the testing period, indicating each wells' production casing was intact. however, initial test pressures at well eh-93 would not stabilize, and pressure dropped off steadily, indicating that eh-93's production casing was communicating with subsurface. (please note that since december 10, 2023, eh-93 has been isolated by downhole temporary plugs). on april 7, 2025, saltville gas completed all plug and abandonment work on well eh-93. the affected casing was removed and sent to a third-party laboratory for analysis. third-party metallurgical test results confirmed that the through-wall defect was primarily caused by microbiologically influenced external corrosion.

NARRATIVE: operator received a call at 1:06am on 2/3/2024 from a resident near sardis ms. resident stated that they heard noise coming from the direction of the pipeline. personnel was dispatched to the site. discovery of the incident occurred at 2:11am. segment was isolated and blown down. upon excavation, three wrinkle bends were found at the incident site. investigation is ongoing; the failed pipe was sent for metallurgical analysis. phmsa has issued cpf2-2024-009-cao. 7/3/2024: the metallurgical analysis was completed in april 2024, with the final report being issued may 29, 2024. the metallurgical analysis concluded that the leak event was caused by the formation of a circumferential crack running along the highest point of a wrinkle bend. metallurgical analysis consisted of visual examination, testing of mechanical properties, chemistry, and charpy impact toughness. based on the tests, all mechanical properties were found to be consistent with api standards at the time of pipeline construction. the two key mechanisms that caused the initiation and growth of these cracks are higher density of hydrogen traps within the id microstructure, as substantiated by the presence of id secondary cracking, in addition to possibly low temperatures. 6/2/2025: the root cause failure analysis (rcfa) and remedial work plan was completed and submitted to phmsa on 7/10/2024. on 3/10/2025, the cao documentation report (cdr) was completed and submitted to phmsa. on 3/28/2025 tennessee gas pipeline company (tgp) received a closure letter from phmsa of the cpf 2-2024-009-cao.

NAME: GOLDEN TRIANGLE STORAGE, LLC
NARRATIVE: on 2/29/24, natural gas compressor unit b (unit b) was stopped during routine shutdown; this action issues a "close" command to unit b's remote actuated suction valve sd2401b. sdv2401b's actuator uses a solenoid valve (versa valve) which is responsible for sdv2401b's actuator operation. the solenoid valve malfunctioned partway through the closure of sdv2401b. shortly after, the scada system alerted the controller that sdv2401b failed to close. the alert was accompanied by additional alarms, 38 alarms in a 40 second period, which included nuisance alarms related to the compressor shutdown as well as alarms from unrelated facility activities. all alarms were acknowledged by the controller. sdv2401b remained in alarm state and sdv2401b was left partially open. a short time later, the controller issued a scada command to stop the compressor building fan system, which, by design, automatically triggers a blow-down of all gas piping inside the compressor building via the facility blow-down system by issuing an 'open' command to bypass valve xxv2404b and blow-down valve bdv2411b. this blow-down process is necessary to ensure the building safe to work in. with sdv2401b still in a partially open position and xxv2404b and bdv2411b in the open position, a flow path was present for gas to continuously flow from the suction side of the compressor unit b to the facility blow-down system, resulting in a continuous release of gas @ 600 mscf/h. on 3/1/2024, the measurement tech recognized an issue with a gas flow totalizer imbalance and then discussed the issue with the on-shift controller. the operations team inspected the facility blow-down system and identified gas venting from the top of the blow-down silencer. immediate action was taken to close the facility's blow-down system and halt the gas release. sdv2401b was stroked to troubleshoot and test what should have been normal function. the actuator solenoid valve (versa valve) was serviced, and proper opening/closure was verified with sdv2401b.

NAME: NORTHWEST PIPELINE LLC
NARRATIVE: on 03/09/2024, at 2:45 am, the cisco compressor station suffered a power outage on the esd system string, triggering an unintended emergency shutdown (esd) resulting in a release of 45 mmcf of natural gas. williams gas control received an alarm indicating the cisco compressor station experienced a facility esd event. the compressor station was pressurized but not running at the time. pipeline control immediately notified operations, who decided to wait until daylight to respond. the decision was based on personal safety risks from navigating the terrain, and the belief that the station was stabilized due to fail-safe vent valves and the suction and discharge isolation valves on the upstream and downstream side of the station. the scada system indicated gas pressure on the mainline segment at cisco compressor station was declining and at 3:45 am, the controller contacted operations to further investigate. an operations technician arrived onsite about an hour later. the technician identified the station discharge valve open and gas venting through the 8" blowdown. pipeline control remotely closed a mainline block valve to limit the release of gas at 6:10 am. the onsite technician manually shut in the facility to stop the gas release at 6:18 am. the operations team performed significant testing and troubleshooting to identify the cause of the esd and the failure of the station discharge valve. this revealed a loose connection on a power jumper wire that supplies power to the esd-related relay strings, which gave the indication of a power loss and triggered the esd. one of the station's discharge valves failed to properly close during the esd due to a solenoid malfunction on the discharge valve. after these causes were identified, function tests were completed prior to returning the compressor station to service.

NAME: ANR PIPELINE CO
NARRATIVE: on march 15, 2024, the monitoring center (mc) received a call from a near-by resident that a vent valve was actively releasing gas at south chester compressor station (cs) in ostega county, near the city of johannesburg, state of michigan. south chester cs is classified as a transmission facility operated and maintained by anr pipeline company, a tc energy entity. mc personnel dispatched a technician to the site to investigate the reported event. the technician arrived at the site at 20:58 edt, shortly thereafter, a second technician arrived to support the first responder. immediate actions were taken to verify that no fire existed in lieu of the unintended release of material into atmosphere, then actions were taken to close the emergency shutdown (esd) valve fv-153. at 21:12 edt, the unintended release of material was stopped. the unintentional gas loss was calculated at 39,419mcf. a call was reported of the incident to the nrc (report no. 1393986). there was no property damage, injuries, fatalities, or mandatory evacuations were needed. the 48hr update report to the nrc (report no. 1394062) was submitted on march 17, 2024. investigation into the shafer actuator discovered an o-ring in the 3-way poppet valve to have failed allowing the pilot gas to vent off which causes the power gas to be applied to the actuator to cycle the valve open as designed. the o-ring has been replaced and the valve was returned back into service on april 1, 2024.

NAME: UGI ENERGY SERVICES
NARRATIVE: the incident took place at farmer brothers metering and regulating station beginning at 20:41 on march 25, 2024. at the facility, natural gas normally flows through a filter separator where any liquids flowing through the separator go to a sump. when the sump level exceeds a certain threshold, the controller actuates the control valve to the open position to release liquids to a waste tank. the control valve's mechanical level controller failed to revert position once the liquid level in the sump had dropped below the design threshold. gas flowed from the separator through a 2" nps pipe into a waste tank and then entered the atmosphere through the tank blowoff valves until the afternoon of march 26, 2024 at 14:45 when the incident was discovered. upon arrival at the facility, personnel immediately shut the manual valve to the liquids tank which ceased emissions of natural gas to the atmosphere at 15:07 on march 26, 2024. the controller on the control valve was found to be misaligned because the spring tension was too high, not allowing the valve to close. the valve's controller was immediately recalibrated, reset, and tested to ensure functionality.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: march 30, 2024, at 0702 hours, passerby notified the emergency call center of venting gas at the la crosse regulator station. gas control was able to confirm a change in pressure, and field operations arrived at 0730 and confirmed the relief venting. after confirming delivery requirements, the relief valve was isolated at 0810. the relief valve and pilot were repaired on site and returned to service march 30, 2024, at 1735 hours. the post investigation determined that the modulating pilot set point was set too close to the normal operating pressure. the cooling effect of reducing pressure through the modulating pilot caused moisture to form and potentially freeze the pilot. since the incident, it was decided to replace the la crosse relief with a higher setting preset by the manufacturer/vendor to avoid future occurrences. the measurement team is identifying locations with similar operating conditions, and they will test and adjust relief set points or replace equipment where applicable.

NARRATIVE: on 3/30/2024 at 2338 hours a local distribution company employee reported that livestock damaged the landowner's farm tap, breaking the 1-inch diameter riser pipe. northern field operations arrived on-site at approximately 0030 on 3/31/2024. farm tap damage with blowing gas was confirmed at 0036 hours. initially it was thought the root valve was the likely leak point. it was determined later that the leak was actually on the 1-inch riser piping. due to the leak being on the 1-inch riser piping, field operations was unable to close the root valve to isolate the farm tap from the pipeline. furthermore, the main gas flow could not be isolated without disrupting service to downstream communities, beemer and west point, nebraska. northern implemented stopple bypass construction to isolate the leak while maintaining gas service to both towns.

NAME: PANHANDLE EASTERN PIPELINE CO
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: at 12:54pm pepl employee received call from a landowner that he could hear a leak and see vapor east of road n and south of 100 rd. at 1:00pm notified employees at olpe station to go to location and confirm leak and location. at 1:15pm the location and leak were confirmed and believed to be the 300l. at 1:17pm sent an employee to protect leak site and two employees to 300l west river header for isolation. at 1:23pm station valve 554-3 was closed. at 1:45pm a gauge was placed on 554-3 dsbo 642psi to confirm the 300l was leaking by pressure drop. at 1:47pm called lyon county dispatch and informed of the situation and location, was asked if assistance was needed, informed them that no assistance was needed at the time. at 1:48pm west river header valve 326w was closed, and at 1:55pm 516 w-1w was opened. at 2:10pm the station pressure was at 569 psi. at 2:17pm valve 516w-2w was opened. at 2:20pm station pressure was at 545 psi. at 2:28pm started blowdown. at 2:38pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 302-e opened. at 2:39pm 2 gate 300-400 crossover valve 402-e opened. at 3:19pm isolated section was blown flat. on 4/11/2024 pipe was exposed, and leak identified as a cracked weld. a 44-foot pipe segment was cut out and replaced. a specimen was sent to the lab for evaluation and determination of cause. the lab report was completed on 11/1/2024 and found that the leak was caused by a combination of a preexisting delayed hydrogen crack on the internal pipe surface at the toe of the girth weld, the presence of a concentrated axial stress at the bottom of the pipe, and the exceedance of the girth weld's tensile strain capacity. the crack measured 34 inches long circumferentially along the bottom side of the girth weld.

NARRATIVE: on april 14, 2024, at 9:43am energy transfer received a notification from the producer sm energy of a possible leak in the area. et personnel arrived on site to investigate at 11:00am. at 11:11am et personnel shut in the briscoe r 21h. this is a 10-inch type c gas gathering line in a rural area located in webb county near laredo, tx. after the line was excavated and exposed, et was able confirm discovery on april 15, 2024 at 9:00am. the location of the leak was discovered at 28.069722, - 99.934444. upon confirmed discovery it was determined that this incident would be reportable due to the estimate of property damage and repair cost. this incident was reported to the nrc on april 15, 2024, at 10:04am an estimated 22.5 mcf of gas was unintentionally released. the line was excavated, and coupons were sent to adv integrity for 3rd party analysis. failures were found to be at the 6 oclock position; two of the pits measured about 1/4-inch in diameter, while the other pit measured 1/8-inch in diameter. sediment was found, removed, and analyzed at the 6 oclock position of the pipeline. the findings showed the sediment had presence of siderite. after reviewing operational and historical records along with a lab analysis we have concluded that the combination of siderite, sand, iron sulfide, and other debris led to under deposit corrosion and to an eventual failure. this line is currently non-piggable . our efforts to mitigate this issue is to modify our quarterly maintenance plan by incorporating chemical treatment for iron sulfide and solid deposits.

NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on 4/16/2024, operations were performing valve maintenance on pl-115 gate valve (wkm valve with an eim actuator). during the close actuation, the valve failed to stop closing when commanded and resulted in the actuator being push off the stem and into the ground. the end of stroke/limit valve failed to isolate power gas after close, resulting in additional torque energy being applied to the gears housing. all that energy resulted in the failure of the cast iron welds between the actuator and yoke/stem housing. with the gear housing off the shaft, the gate valve could not remain closed and pipeline pressure slammed it open against the bonnet. as a result of the actuator failure, a stainless power gas line broke off and vented. the eim actuator controls were tested on a bench with pressurized air and discovered to successfully achieve the open limit but not the close limit. the cause for this was the close limit valve was installed backwards, which resulted in the poppet being unable to engage with the cam and failure to isolate power gas to the motor once the valve was closed.

NAME: MOUNTAINWEST PIPELINE, LLC
NARRATIVE: on 4/23/2024 williams reported an event to the nrc due to the total volume of gas release exceeding 3 mmscf. the total volume released that day was 17.76 mmscf totaling between two psv's on mainline 40 at the jl40-47 junction and green river meter station, but both released gas due to the same cause. at the time of the initial release operations was on site performing other work at the jl40-47 junction. at the time of the release there were two compressor stations that were down for maintenance, this left only one compressor station available in the area to move gas. an issue on the fuel control valve with the compressor that was running caused repeated shutdowns. these repeated shutdowns caused gas to backup on the system and pressures built up, ultimately causing the two psv's to lift on the mainline resulting in the gas release that was reported. the fuel valves were operated in safe mode to subvert a powered hour limitation set by solar to keep flow through on the line, however they had to be restarted every hour to maintain this.

NAME: TENNESSEE GAS PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on april 29, 2024 tgp experienced a reportable unplanned esd at compressor station 25 due to lightning in the area. one esd valve in the yard did not close due to an outage on the 100-2 line. fuel gas to valve was disconnected for outage and when the esd was triggered gas was not able to get to the valve to operate. at cleveland, power gas is needed to operate the valves. a separate esd power gas operates the esd valves when an esd is activated. the valve did not close as expected because there was not power gas in the esd. the investigation discovered that that the esd system design did not include sending esd power gas into this valve. tgp is installing the connection to send esd power gas. 28,100 mcf of natural gas lost. fire department did show up to site but was not needed.

NARRATIVE: on 04-26-2024, at 5:37 am central time, enterprise observed a pressure drop on the 20-inch mivida trunk c pipeline in ward county, texas. the incident occurred southwest of pyote, texas. on 5:38 am, enterprise personnel were dispatched to the pipeline to determine its status. at 05:57 am, enterprise personnel reported a fire in the general direction of the mivida trunk c pipeline. the actual time of ignition is unknown. at 6:15 am, enterprise arrived at the lease road near the pipeline scene. local emergency responders were already at the scene. it was determined that the fire was located at a crossing with a 3rd party pipeline, which was also on fire. at 6:19 am, enterprise personnel determined that the fire impacted enterprise mivida trunk c pipeline. between 6:20 am and 7:17 am, the pipeline was isolated. at 7:15 am, enterprise determined that the fire from the pipeline met incident reporting criteria and the nrc/trrc were notified at 7:33 am and 7:47 am respectively. a review of scada trends indicated the pressure drop started at 05:15 am. on 04-30-2024, at 15:45 pm, the fire self-extinguished. the pipeline was placed back into service on 05-21-2024. a metallurgical analysis determined that the cause of the incident was internal corrosion of the pipeline at the 6:00 o'clock position.

NARRATIVE: on april 26, 2024, at approximately 05:20 am, a rupture occurred involving a third-party gas pipeline facility. this event occurred approximately 270 feet from atmos energys above ground station at the terminus of its transmission line, line x2-7, which was not connected to the subject ruptured facilities. the rupture damaged a pipe support at atmos energys above ground station and caused it to sink into the soil, which then caused a 12-inch valve flange to misalign resulting in a release of natural gas and subsequent fire. at 07:15 am, atmos energy was notified of the event by another involved third-party operator. the first atmos energy technician arrived on site and determined the condition to exist at approximately 07:49 am. although atmos energy was unable to approach the station yard at this time because of the ongoing event, confirmed discovery was determined at 09:17 am based upon the anticipated station damage cost. atmos energys gas controllers, in coordination with atmos energys onsite employees, closed valves to isolate line x2-7 and the upstream lateral line x2 from the atmos energy trunkline at 8:10 am. both connected lines were allowed to blow down at a safe distance from the damaged facility. the fire at the station was allowed to burn out, which occurred at approximately 12:45 pm. on may 3, 2024, the x2 valve at line x2-7 was closed separating these two lines. on may 22, 2024, the upstream lateral line x2 was placed back in service. the damaged station and the entire 263 feet of line x2-7 will not be replaced or placed back into service.

NAME: TRUNKLINE GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on april 30, 2024 at approximately 5:52 pm, gas control received an alarm and dispatched ete personnel to the longville compressor station. ete found the esd system had been set off and the station was blowing gas. main fire gate valve did not seal off and continued to blow gas for an additional forty-three minutes until employees determined which fire gate valve was causing the station not to blow down. it was determined that the esd system was triggered by a faulty wire caused the gas detection system to the south gas detector on 4509 to indicate a false reading with up to 50% lel and over range. after further investigation, it was determined at 4:15 pm on may 1, 2024 approximately 67.68 mmscf of natural gas was released to the atmosphere. main fire gate plug valve was disassembled, inspected, reassembled and greased, tested for functionality and sealing off against positive pressure. equipment was returned to service. supplemental/final -updated time in a4 & a16a -updated c3 to valve
