NAME: TRANSCONTINENTAL GAS PIPE LINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: an accidental ignition occurred at station 60 on may 8, 2024, an interstate transmission compressor station operated by transcontinental pipe line company, llc (transco) near jackson, louisiana. at the time, station 60 was offline and isolated from operating pipelines for scheduled maintenance to replace internal valve components connecting the compressor units to the station's common suction and discharge headers. the incident happened at 6:32 am, just before scheduled maintenance work was to begin for that day. the facility's construction provided for single valve isolation between each pipeline and facility piping. work plans anticipated leakage at these isolation points and incorporated an air purge plan to mitigate potential flammable environments within piping. the root cause investigation determined that the following causes directly led to the consequences of this incident: 1. flammable material (natural gas) leaked into the station piping around the process isolation between the station and transmission pipelines; 2. the mitigative air flow did not maintain flammable gas concentration below the lel; 3. the mitigative air flow dried internal sludge deposits inside the station piping; 4. suspected accumulation of pyrophoric iron sulfide in the internal sludge deposits of the station piping ignited upon exposure to oxygen; and 5. a person was present within the fire zone at the time of the accidental ignition. to prevent similar issues from recurring, williams is committed to following the recommendations derived from the root cause analysis. this includes providing comprehensive guidance and conducting refresher training for all personnel involved. by reinforcing the knowledge and skills necessary for safe operations, williams aims to ensure that personnel are equipped to recognize potential hazards and respond appropriately. phmsa reviewed williams return to service plan and approved on june 18th, 2024. williams station 60 returned to service on june 22nd at 9:55 am

NAME: ENABLE OKLAHOMA INTRASTATE TRANSMISSION, LLC
CAUSE_DETAILS: DEFECTIVE OR LOOSE TUBING OR FITTING
NARRATIVE: 5/19/24 13:04, operator received a report of gas venting at claremore compressor station. technician was dispatched to the station to investigate report. on 5/19/24 at 13:40, technician arrival at the station. technician identified unit 427 discharge relief valve venting into the yard silencer. at 14:00, technician notified system control of the incident. technician enters the building and takes unit 427 offline and isolated the unit. 14:07, technician notified system control of the problem and instructed them to start up unit 428 and put it online to replace unit 427. upon investigation of the failure, technician identified a tubing sensing line, that went to the unit relief valve, had failed resulting in the cause of the relief valve venting. at 14:20, technician started gathering data to determine the amount of gas loss that was vented during this incident. at 14:55, it was determined that the gas loss for the incident was 8,475 mscf making this a reportable incident. at 15:03, dot compliance was notified of the reportable incident. at 15:23, notification was made to the national response center (incident report # 1399561). on 05/20/24 at 08:00, tubing line was replaced (with a high-pressure flex steel line to prevent incident from recurring again in the future), relief valve was retested and put back in service.

NAME: BEAR CREEK STORAGE CO
NARRATIVE: after reviewing the timeline of events and the factual evidence, the investigation team concluded that while there was not definitive evidence that circulation of the well would have prevented this incident, it appears that the gas release occurred as a result of well fluid imbalance. had the well remediation process required circulation of the well fluid, conditions in the well may not have reached a state of imbalance, which ultimately led to the loss of well control. therefore, the well remediation procedure was determined to be inadequate. the full root cause failure analysis was submitted to phmsa on november 19, 2024.

NAME: SOUTHERN STAR CENTRAL GAS PIPELINE, INC
NARRATIVE: on 5/6/2024 an ef4 tornado struck the city of barnsdall, oklahoma at approximately 9:45 pm cdt. sscgp meter facilities for the city of barnsdall setting 3417 and the wax refinery 3416 (both settings are at the same location) were damaged. sscgp employees were able to access the site at 12:14 am. a leak was discovered on the meter run and the above ground valves were immediately closed. due to the damage of the primary meter runs, the by-pass to the city was opened to provide un-interrupted service to barnsdall and is being utilized until temporary metering facilities are installed. service to the wax refinery was shut off due to extensive damage to the wax refinery. temporary metering facilities will be installed to serve the wax refinery when natural gas service is requested by the refinery. the full scale of the damage to the meter facilities was not able to be evaluated immediately due to debris and site conditions. at approximately 8:00 am on 5/7/2024, a preliminary evaluation was made, it was determined that the operator's property damage would exceed the incident threshold of $139,700. a notification was made to the nrc on 5/7/2024 at 8:47 am. sscgp is currently scoping a project to replace all of the above ground facilities at this location.

NARRATIVE: on thursday, may 9th at approximately 1:25pm central time, emmet operations received a call from a third party about a possible line strike with a gas release. at 1:38pm, operations personnel confirmed that a third party had struck line sm-23 with a bulldozer causing a gas release. no one was injured and the gas did not ignite. an operations technician remained on site to monitor the release while one technician went to the upstream valve site and another technician mobilized to the downstream valve site. pressure at the time of the strike was 550psig; pressure was lowered to 350psig and monitored. the decision to monitor pressure was made to avoid significant outages to residential customers. once customer notifications were finalized, the pipeline was shunt in and blown down. a type b sleeve was installed over the defect and the pipeline was purged and returned to service on friday may 10th at approximately 4:40pm central time. the pipeline was struck by a third party logging company. the contractors working for the logging company did not complete a one call and were not authorized to perform work on the sm-23 right of way.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on may 20, 2024, an incident occurred on pipeline sr- 538 in benton, ohio, during a scheduled maintenance project. as part of the project, four (4) tc energy technicians and two (2) third party contractors were working to install a skillet blind flange to isolate the affected pipeline segment. the crew observed a gas leak from a 6-inch valve at that time and decided to grease the valve to remediate the leak using a motorized grease gun. an ignition/flash fire ensued that injured two (2) of the tc energy technicians and both of the third-party contractors. the injured workers were immediately taken for medical evaluation and treatment. tc energy completed an investigation to identify the factors that may have caused or contributed to the incident. the results of that investigation identified the following proposed recommendations: 1. develop and publish an operating procedure, or update existing procedures, to outline the requirements for installing a skillet blind. 2. conduct a control of work assessment for installing skillet blinds to produce a hazard controls diagram for review by personnel with the job safety analysis (jsa). 3. implement improvements to personnel training materials to provide more emphasis on the adequate response to unexpected leaks. 4. conduct risk assessment on the usage of csn solutions black widow 20v grease guns. 5. update the jsa form to have operator confirm the specific personal protective equipment (ppe) needed for the task (e.g., flame-resistant clothing, etc.) 6. update applicable procedures to require a hot work permit to be completed when installing a skillet blind downstream of a single point of isolation regardless of whether a gas leak occurs. 7. complete ongoing effort to issue personal diffusive 4-gas monitor gas monitors to all tc energy field technicians and operations specialists. 8. update jsa form to clarify that contractors must also sign the jsa if they are also involved in the task being covered. 9. share additional details and learnings from the incident to the organization. 10. update gas handling procedures to clarify the amount of time since the last valve inspection / servicing that would trigger additional inspection / servicing before completing a lockout tag out activity. tc energy sent the valve associated with the incident to a laboratory for further analysis. the lab result confirmed the source of the gas leak was the valve. the following are the result of tests; 1-the seat tests conducted in general accordance with the 24th edition of api 6d, specification for pipeline and piping valves, showed that there was a detectable leak at the valve seat of the subject plug valve at pressures as low as 70 psi. 2-the shell tests conducted in general accordance with the 24th edition of api 6d showed that there was a detectable leak at the flanged connection between the rotating shaft of the plug and the shell of the valve at pressures as low as 800 psi.

NAME: FLORIDA GAS TRANSMISSION CO
CAUSE_DETAILS: VALVE LEFT OR PLACED IN WRONG POSITION, BUT NOT RESULTING IN AN OVERPRESSURE
NARRATIVE: on 05/31/2024 at 18:12, the 12-inch station discharge header blowdown inadvertently opened resulting in gas blowing at approximately 1100 psi for 78 minutes. a local emergency responder notified the control center in houston, tx. control center called local operations management and an fgt employee was dispatched to compressor station 27 thonotosassa and found the discharge blowdown open. the employee immediately closed the manual block valve just downstream of the automatic valve. upon further investigation, the employee found a three-way valve on the esd line in the closed position. seals in the operator on the discharge blowdown valve had been replaced on the previous day. there are two valves inline on the esd sensing feed line. the cause of the incident was due to a valve left or placed in wrong position, but not resulting in an overpressure. replacing 3-way-switching valve with a manual block valve in line with a manual bleed between the two block valves to prevent potential reoccurrence.

NAME: UGI UTILITIES, INC
NARRATIVE: on may 30, 2024, a body vent fitting on an above-ground 12-inch valve began leaking to atmosphere after it was operated as part of an in-line inspection of a natural gas transmission pipeline. the 12-inch valve was associated with the isolation of a pig receiver location involved in the in-line inspection project. the leak was continuously monitored by ugi personnel until the valve was replaced on june 18, 2024. on july 7, 2025, a supplemental and final report is being filed to provide updated incident information. ugi consulted with the valve manufacturer who examined and investigated the valve. ugi subsequently performed a root cause analysis of the event. ugi concluded that the root cause of this event was attributable to the valve seals that were exposed to debris such as weld slag. weld slag was found embedded into the seals and did not allow the valve to seal completely. the body bleed valve also did not seal and was stripped while being operated and leaked continuously to atmosphere for a short duration. ugi was able to stop the leak until the final repair could be made. based on the small opening of the body bleed valve, the escaping gas was negligible.

NAME: BBT SIGCO INTRASTATE, LLC
NARRATIVE: on 6/17/2024 bubbling was seen from a third-party helicopter pilot. the pilot reported the situation to bbt which they investigated and confirmed on 6/18/2024 to be the 16" bbt pipeline. bbt initially treated it as a src due to the nature of the event (slow leak) and the vicinity (in the marsh, 1.5 miles from the nearest building), but was elevated to an incident within an hour when it was determined it was going to exceed the regulatory requirement in becoming an incident on 6/28/2024 (due to the mobilization cost and equipment needed in the marsh) . the leak was isolated immediately, and discussions were made to minimize fugitive emissions. as a result, customers burned down the gas to the regulator set point (200psi). the remaining gas was blown down to initiate repairs. repairs started on 6/24/2024 (weld-on sleeve) and the pipeline was returned to service on 7/1/2024. localized pitting was determined to be the cause in-between the concrete coatings near the seams where coal tar is the coating.

NAME: COLUMBIA GULF TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on june 25, 2024, at approximately 03:00 hrs. edt, tc energy gas control received a scada callout-station alarm, esd alarm, 106 alarm for the stanton compressor station. tc energy operations personnel arrived at the stanton compressor station, located in powell county, kentucky, and discovered that unit 106 had esd'd as designed. it was determined that the incident occurred as result of metal wear within the turbine diffuser housing of unit 106. the metal wear allowed heat to escape and allowed surrounding electrical equipment, such as, wiring, transmitters, and conduit to smolder and melt. the incident was identified by the station's fixed temperature detector system and therefore initiated the esd of unit 106. unit 106 was shut down due to the incident and is currently shut down until repairs can be made. the stanton compressor station, as a whole, was not shut down due to this incident.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on july 2, 2024, a fire occurred at the oasis waha compressor station, 2.26 miles north of coyanosa, texas in pecos county. at approximately 0500 scada notified operations about a unit down on fire detection. 0520, it was discovered that compressor units 3 & 4 were on fire, esdd the station and called the local fire department to the station. at 0543, it was determined the repairs and damages would exceed the $145,400.00 reportable dollar criteria and the nrc and the txrrc was notified. local fire department extinguished the fire. the damaged compressors were bypassed, and the station was back online on july 5. fuel gas and line oil fueled the fire. the cause of the fire is still under investigation. a supplemental report will be submitted once investigation is complete. **during the physical inspection there were also found to be broken bolts gathered for analysis. the coupling cover bolt, as well as a missing bolt from the turbine drain flange were found on the skid floor. these bolts were also sent to metallurgist also and were determined to have failed due to fatigue. the sheared bolt and staining on the drain flange suggest a possible root cause of the fire. the failure of the flange as an oil sealing mechanism would lead to oil draining directly onto the exhaust blanket leading to vaporization and ignition of the oil. this was an isolated incident. the mitigation steps to prevent this from occurring in the future are as followed: -evaluate fire eyes/gas detector placement on these packages. -change fasteners on engine swings. -coordinate an evaluation of all units to confirm no missing/broken fasteners, this is now included in our 4000-hour preventative maintenance plan.

NAME: EQUITRANS MIDSTREAM CORPORATION
NARRATIVE: at 22:54 on 7/4/2024, compliance received a call indicating that gas was leaking past a check valve on the discharge side of the compressor, which caused a relief valve to go off, and gas to migrate to a unit that had shut down earlier in the day. that unit was shut down for a different reason unrelated to the cause of this incident. the shut down unit has a safety feature that vents all gas through the blowdown stack. the venting started to occur at approximately 4:30 and stopped at approximately 10:35, resulting in an approximate loss of 7,771 mcf of gas lost (updated from 7,500 mcf on the nrc reports). when operations arrived on site, a ball valve was shut upstream of the unit to block any more gas from being vented. on monday, 7/8, operations inspected the check valve and found a teflon bolt stuck in the valve. once the bolt was removed, the valve was able to operate normally. the teflon bolt holds the compressor valve cages in the cylinder of the compressor. these bolts are kept in the compressor per the compressor manufacturer's design. the bolts are not meant to be removed under any circumstance. going forward, the technicians will inspect the bolts during compressor maintenance for secure fit, wear, and damage. they will be replaced as needed. the company will review its procedures to determine if any changes are necessary.

NAME: PACIFIC GAS & ELECTRIC CO
NARRATIVE: on wednesday, july 10, 2024, at approximately 21:04 hours, pg&e incident on-duty personnel confirmed a release of gas at kettleman compressor station resulted in an injury necessitating in-patient hospitalization. following completion of construction, clearance activities to re-introduce gas and purge air from the system, initiated: - the approved clearance required v-56 to be "checked open" for purging, however, it had been closed for stem seal replacement work on july 8, 2024, and only partially opened prior to the purge - operations that had not been documented nor approved as part of the sequence of operations in the clearance. - gas was re-introduced to the system from a 34'' control valve (v-90), a clearance point with 618 psi. there are two ways to operate v-90, manual hydraulic and manual pneumatic. - when attempting to manually operate v-90 hydraulically, oil unexpectedly discharged from the actuator's manual hydraulic override system relief valve and the valve failed to operate. - v-90 was then partially opened using the manual pneumatic controls. this method is not effective for fine throttling as required for purging in design standard a-38. gas from v-90 began to displace air at multiple vent locations per the established clearance plan. it is suspected that as a result of the partial open position of v-56, a greater amount of gas flow was directed toward v-78. instead of gas exiting the 1/2'' vertical vent valve downstream of v-78 as approved in the clearance, gas exited the full 6'' pipe opening horizontally where the blind flange had been removed on july 9. gas flowed directly into an opposing blind flange roughly 20'' away at v-79. this resulted in deflection in all directions, including into the excavation below. a hazardous air-gas plume developed. at approximately 18:42 hours, the air-gas plume ignited, resulting in serious burns to one coworker and minor injuries to others. cws in the area immediately responded, packer out of the wellbore in approximately 3 to 5 seconds. the gas that built up between the two downhole barriers was released. in less than thirty seconds, the onsite crews secured the well with NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on july 15, 2024, a rupture occurred on energy transfer companys k to coya 24-inch pipeline located approximately 15 miles southwest of monahans, tx. at 3:30 a.m. supervisory control and data acquisition (scada) system alerted the coyanosa gas plant operator of a loss of pressure. at 4:40 a.m. the pipeline operator arrived on location to find local first responders were already on scene battling a fire. the emergency personnel had been notified of the fire by a third party. at 5:20 a.m. the affected pipeline was isolated, and the fire had burned out, energy transfer personnel were able to confirm the discovery of a rupture on the k to coya 24. it was determined the repairs and damages would exceed the $145,400.00 reportable dollar criteria and the nrc and the txrrc were notified. the local fire department allowed the fire to burn itself out. the cause of the rupture is still under investigation. the cause of the rupture was identified as external corrosion occurring along the 3:00 oclock side of the pipe. the thinnest measured remaining wall thickness was determined to be 0.020-inch (7% of the nominal wall thickness). other areas of corrosion present on the pipe material provided appeared consistent with dc interference current corrosion and under deposit corrosion. plan to prevent recurrence, operations will install more cp test stations to help locate external corrosion trouble areas and install more rectifiers to impress current equally over the entirety of the pipeline. operations will also utilize corrosion coupons and chemical injection to monitor and mitigate any internal corrosion.

NARRATIVE: during routine pigging operation to remove hydrocarbon liquids and water from a 60-psig gas gathering pipeline, the fluids were decanted in a controlled manner into a temporary atmospheric storage (frac) tank. operating procedures did not address the need to establish a safety zone (visual warnings and windsocks) around the pipeline pigging operation area to help to eliminate random ignition sources in an area expected to have temporary exposure to hydrocarbon vapors. ultimately, it was a vehicle which was parked too close to the work area which provided the ignition source when an employee entered the vehicle and turned the ignition key. the release of hydrocarbon vapors was the expected result of the controlled depressurizing of a stream of hydrocarbon liquids into an atmospheric storage vessel, which had no means of vapor containment. additionally, a vapor control and discharge plan was not utilized during the process. the root cause of the fire was a failure of operating procedures in allowing a potential source of ignition (a vehicle) to be located within an area expected to be temporarily exposed to evolved hydrocarbon vapors. this incident was not the result of any pipeline material failure, abnormal operating conditions (i.e., overpressure condition), or incidental third-party damage to the pipeline facilities.

NARRATIVE: on friday afternoon 9/20/24 at 13:21 ct, a technician at the monroe gas storage compressor station observed small bubbles rising within a puddle of water while doing regular inspection rounds within the fenced facility. after confirming the presence of natural gas at the location and suspecting a pinhole leak, the 18" eastside gas transmission line was isolated by manually closing the downstream valves. because the line was not flowing at the time, the upstream valves were already closed. the effected line segment was isolated by 14:13 ct. after initial coordination regarding possible cost of repair, it was determined to classify the event as an incident and notify the national response center (nrc). the nrc was notified by the williams security operations center at 15:27 ct. the pipeline was safely blown down with lock out / tag out completed by 19:20 ct that evening. due to the pipeline's 10' depth in the area, it took multiple days for contractors to clean the line through cleaning pigs, purge with nitrogen and pothole through hydrovacing to pinpoint the leak location. once identified (through detecting the presence of nitrogen), the leak location was fully and safely excavated (considering the significant depth) on 10/14/24. as of 10/15/24, internal corrosion was found at the pinhole leak location. the effected pipe immediately near the leak location was cut-out on 10/17/24 and sent to a lab for analysis. williams operations, pipeline integrity and construction teams established a conservative plan to replace necessary pipe and return the line to service. approximately 350 feet of 18-inch pipe in the low area of the pipeline (within the facility) was replaced and hydrotested. the line was returned to service on 11/9/2024. the cause is suspected to be sulfate reducing bacteria microbiologically influenced corrosion (srb-mic) based on lab results. representatives from operations, management and pipeline integrity have established an internal corrosion mitigation plan to prevent reoccurrence. coupons have been installed at each well head location and other locations, based on internal corrosion data gathered, operations, management, compliance and corrosion department will deem if more locations are needed. a pigging program that includes all 13 laterals is forthcoming, with additional focus on the 18" lateral.

NAME: BLUEWATER GAS STORAGE, LLC
NARRATIVE: re: omo rd compressor station incident nrc incident report #1413461 & follow up #1413594 on october 5, 2024 at approximately 3:09 am, emergency shutdown (esd) vent valves (bdv 9010) and (bdv 9011) opened because of a loss of power gas pressure used to hold the esd valves closed. pipeline isolation (sdv-9001) was also open, resulting in a gas release of ~5.2 mmscf to atmosphere. the loss of power gas was caused by of a combination of an isolation of the power gas header and a leaking regulator in the power gas system. on october 3, 2024, at 10:56 a.m., the fuel gas supply valve (sdv 9008) tripped / closed due to high pressure (>475 psig). the high pressure was caused by daytime heating and thermal expansion of the gas in the fuel gas system. the omo road compressor station was shutdown at the time, minimizing fuel gas use and causing fuel gas header pressure to fluctuate with ambient temperature. in addition to its primary function to supply fuel to the natural gas fired engines used to drive the gas compressors at the station, the fuel gas system also provides power gas to the power gas header. typically, power gas pressure is high enough that the gas pressure overcomes the spring tension used to open the blowdown valves in the event of an esd. following the overpressure condition, sdv 9008 was not reopened because the compressor station was idle and the need for fuel gas was minimal. with sdv 9008 closed and the power gas header isolated, a leaking regulator on bdv 9011 eventually bled off enough pressure from the power gas header to allow bdv 9010 and bdv 9011 to fail open as designed. the leaking regulator was identified following the release on october 5, 2024 and repaired on october 17, 2024. corrective action: bluewater will implement corrective actions to preclude repetition of the incident, minimize the amount of vented gas, and improve reporting timeliness. 1. update procedures to avoid the isolation of the power gas header: a. option 1: sdv 9008 (fuel gas supply) will be open during normal and stand by operations b. option 2: (tbd) vb-9071 changed to 'normally open' to provide an uninterrupted supply to the power gas header 2. control logic at the site allowed for the pipeline valve (supply gas) to remain open when the vent valves bdv 9010 and bdv 9011 were open. a. bluewater has updated logic at the facility, if a vent valve is in any position other than "closed" the pipeline valve feeding the facility (sdv 9001) will close. 3. scada alarms to improve response time will be added. a. "valves out of sequence" notifying the operator that the vent valve and the pipeline valves are open or in travel. b. "low pipeline pressure" an adjustable alarm the operators can set for the current operating conditions on the pipelines. c. "low low pipeline pressure" a non-adjustable "high priority" alarm set at 650 psig. 4. revise emergency procedures to include volumetric thresholds for reporting natural gas releases to federal and state agencies consistent with existing rules and regulations. 5. training: additional/refresher training on reporting requirements i.e. time to report, and thresholds for reporting. bluewater completed the training for appropriate employees on october 15, 2024.

NAME: GREAT BASIN GAS TRANSMISSION COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on wednesday, october 9, 2024, aspen developers corporation (aspen developers) was operating a track hoe to complete road work (grading and drainage) in preparation for a water line installation in the sierra nevada mountains, approximately 3.5 miles east of the washoe county census-designated place of incline village, nevada. while performing work on the existing dirt road, the track hoe operator punctured the top of great basin gas transmission company's (great basin) 8-inch diameter north tahoe lateral gas pipeline with a tooth of the track hoe bucket. the damage occurred at the approximate milepost location of nt-13.56 and resulted in the unintentional release of gas from the steel transmission facility. great basin received notification of the damage at approximately 16:00 pdt on october 9, 2024, by truckee meadows fire and rescue, and promptly dispatched emergency response personnel to the scene for additional investigation and remediation. the pipeline and hazardous material safety administration (phmsa) notification was made to the national response center (nrc) on october 9, 2024, at 20:14 pdt and assigned incident #1413294 due to the natural gas release anticipated to exceed three million cubic feet. great basin did not shutdown the facility to avoid service interruption to a downstream shipper (local distribution company). a repair clamp was used to control the flow of gas on october 10, 2024, at 20:49 pdt. a supplemental notification was made to the nrc on october 14, 2024, at 09:08 pdt and assigned incident #1413672. great basin calculated the total release of gas to total 7,304 mcf . great basin performed a preliminary internal investigation to determine contributing factors associated with the incident on october 16, 2024, and determined that the facility locate marks, established on august 28, 2024, deviated from the actual facility location by 19 feet and the locator incorrectly marked the facility due to bleed off onto a nearby, unmarked steel water line. great basin also determined that the facility locate ticket (2024081500260) used by aspen developers was expired as of september 12, 2024. in addition, and as required by great basin through documentation and verbal communications with the excavator, aspen developers did not notify great basin in advance of excavation to request a high pressure standby, nor did aspen developers pothole great basin facilities to verify location and depth. the repair clamp great basin installed on october 10, 2024 to control the flow of gas was welded onto the impacted area as a permanent repair on october 25, 2024.

NARRATIVE: on november 3, 2024, at 9:22 pm, the control center discovered a loss of communication with the claude compressor unit. the operations team arrived at the claude, texas, compressor station (station no. tx-083) at 10:30 pm and discovered that the 8-inch blowdown/vent was open. the inlet and outlet valves to the compressor did not fully close causing gas to keep entering the compressor and escaping through the vent valve. the side valves were closed by 10:37 pm and the venting stopped. the operations team determined that the compressor unit's program logic controllers went down causing the loss in communication. the compressor then shutdown and vented as it was supposed to do. the plcs went down due to the main power supplies shorting out. the compressor was able to be brought back online at 12:29 am on 11/4/2024. the cause of the power supply short is still under investigation.

NARRATIVE: a transmission line leak was identified in ego's gas storage system (group 8) at approximately 16:15 edt on 10/18/2024 near 9232 mudbrook st nw in jackson, oh after a member of the public called in an odor complaint. local personnel utilized valves to shut in the leaking line around 18:00 edt that same day. an original assessment of the costs to replace the line were under the $145,400 operator loss threshold for an incident per 191.3. on 11/5/2024 at approximately 9:20 est, the enbridge gas ohio project manager for the replacement of the section of pipe with the leak informed pipeline safety that costs were now likely to eventually exceed the $145,400 threshold due to higher than expected environmental and contractor costs. the leak was called in as an incident at that time to the ohio public utility commission and the national response center. the section of pipe with the leak has been removed and sent to a 3rd party for analysis. a new section of pipe has been installed to replace the old line but is not yet in service. a supplemental report will be provided with the in-service date and results of the 3rd party lab analysis. 4/25/25 supplemental update: laboratory analysis has been completed. the results of the metallurgical analysis indicate that the leak occurred at an area of discrete pitting from internal corrosion at the bottom of the pipe (6:17 orientation). the leak was likely caused by the presence of an acidic brine (ph 2.92, measured at ambient pressure) with high salinity. the localized corrosion likely occurred at breaks in an otherwise thick protective scale or at areas under deposits at the bottom of the pipe. it is possible that there was a gas phase contribution (i.e., from co2, h2s, and/or 02 corrosion), however, the gas phase contribution was likely secondary to the presence of the acidic brine. the cause of the brine acidity at this location is unknown, but a ph value of 2.92, measured at ambient pressure, is in excess of what is possible from co2 gas dissolved in the process stream. enbridge gas ohio has placed permanent ut gauges on the line for future internal corrosion monitoring. pipeline was placed back into service on 1/7/25. 5/12/2025 updated final report: a14 was changed to "onshore pipeline" to reflect that pipe was considered a transmission asset for regulatory purposes. 5/20/2025: finalizing supplemental report with changes to a14. 1/12/2026: updated final report: c1 was changed from "interstate" to "intrastate".

NARRATIVE: on 11/05/2024 at approximately 04:45, due to an increasing flow rate that could not be controlled with a set point change, gas control called a technician to investigate the regulators at the efm 4 to net mexico meter station. upon arrival, the technician found the station blowing gas to the atmosphere and discovered a broken 1" nipple on the #2 regulator run. at approximately 06:00, the technician shut the upstream manual valve and verified that the downstream pneumatic valve was closed. the technician then throttled the #1 regulator to achieve the desired set point given by gas control. at 06:30, the technician replaced the nipple with an xxh nipple, installed a new 1" valve, reconnected the tubing, and returned the station to normal service.

CAUSE_DETAILS: EXCAVATION DAMAGE BY OPERATOR'S CONTRACTOR (SECOND PARTY)
NARRATIVE: summary of event on saturday, november 9, 2024, at 1:33 pm local time (central standard time) a contractor performing work for people's gas light & coke (pgl) was doing excavation work adjacent to county road 2700 north at approximate latitude/longitude 40.266609/-88.432686. while performing the excavation work with a backhoe, at the completion of a swipe, the operator heard a pop/hiss and observed gas blowing into the air. the natural gas transmission line being excavated was at approximately 1,750 psig. the contractor personnel contacted pgl employees working in the vicinity. pgl responded with on shift personnel augmented by off work employees. the area was made safe and the leak was isolated using manual transmission line valves. the affected pipeline was isolated at approximately 3:00 pm and was depressurized to atmospheric pressure at 3:30 pm. at 4:50 pm, pgl estimated the release to exceed 3,000,000 standard cubic feet (scf). pgl notified the national response center (nrc) at 5:06 pm and the illinois commerce commission (icc) at 5:29 pm. a follow up call was made to the nrc on monday, november 11, 2024 at 2:43 pm, during which pgl reported a calculated release volume of 4.953 mmcf. causes the direct cause of the release was damage caused by the backhoe shovel contact to surrounding soil and/or installed equipment including the following: a 1" 3,000 psig rated, threaded w-k-m dynaseal quarter turn ball valve installed at the 12 o'clock position on the 12" carbon steel transmission pipeline. on one end (toward atmosphere) of this valve was a 1" hex head plug and on the other end (leading to the 12" pipeline), was a 1"x3" schedule 160 nipple that was screwed into a thread-o-let that was welded to the pipeline. the root cause was as-built drawings were not updated to reflect the above equipment following installation in march 2024. drawings were not updated because the installation was thought to be temporary in nature to support future purging operations that would be needed for planned construction. because drawings were not updated, information regarding installation of the equipment was not available to the personnel performing excavation activities. contributing to the event was the backhoe operator performing excavation within the tolerance zone of 18" of the pipeline. the backhoe operator's operator qualification was removed because of the incident and is pending remediation and requalification. amount of gas released: based on further calculations using relief valve capacity methodology, pgl has revised the calculated release volume to be 5,163,905 scf. this includes 4,842,969 scf prior to isolation and 320,936 scf following isolation. a 1.25" opening was used during the calculation. this opening provides a conservative calculation related to the 1" threadolet connection, which was forcibly removed by the backhoe and/or adjacent soil being compressed during excavation. actions taken 1. all work associated with the project was shutdown pending pgl investigation. 2. direction provided to pgl and contract resources that w-k-m dynasealvalves will not be buried in the future. a plan was developed to address other locations where these style valves have been installed. (update: other locations with valves installed with the same configuration have been removed). 3. directed pgl and contract resources that anything being installed on pgl facilities is required to be documented in the as-built drawings. 4. directed contract resources that only hand digging will occur inside of the 18 inch tolerance zone. 5. informed contract resources that any hit that results in a release of gas the excavator must call 911 and julie must be notified.

NAME: GULF SOUTH PIPELINE COMPANY, LLC
NARRATIVE: on 11/24/24 at approximately 20:56, a pipeline rupture occurred on gulf south's bistineau storage field well line a-11, also referred to as index 900-8. the rupture was initially identified by a gulf south operations employee who lives onsite. the bi-directional 8-inch o.d. well line connects the single a-11 well to the a lateral pipeline trunk between the compressor station field header and the storage field. the a-11 well was shut in, along with the corresponding valves located on the a lateral trunk pipeline, allowing gulf south to totally isolate the affected well line from the storage field and compressor station field header. this enabled the affected line segment to be fully depressurized. the line segment remained isolated and depressurized until a pipe replacement was completed. repair was completed on 12/11/24 by pipe replacement. the failed section of pipe and a short pup from each end of the remaining pipe were inspected on site by gulf south's metallurgist, wrapped, and sent to a lab for further analysis which has not yet been completed. the field examination determined the preliminary cause of the failure to be internal corrosion. additionally, phmsa asked how this pipeline is treated. it is treated using a continuous injection pump. a corrosion inhibitor, specifically coastal chemical 1141-c, is injected when the field is in withdrawal mode. on average, 0.25 to 0.5 gallons per day of chemical is pumped. 1/24/25 updated response to c3g and part h per phmsa request.

NARRATIVE: 11/18/2024 at 13:30 hours, a pipeline operator was conducting a routine inspection and discovered a leak on pipeline m2115-1. the pipeline was isolated and less than 3 mmcf was released. the pipeline was excavated, and a crack was located near in the heat affected zone of a fillet weld at the 6 o'clock position. the crack was on the 30" mainline piping adjacent to a spherical tee that was installed for a pipeline hot tap. determination was made that the repair would exceed the reporting threshold of $145,400 and notification was made to the nrc at 11:20 am on 11/19/24. the spherical tee was removed, and a barred tee was installed on sunday,11/24/24. the pipeline was placed back into service on monday, 11/25/24. a third-party failure analysis was performed on the component. the root cause was identified as an issue in the welding process. contributing factors included insufficient pre-heat and lack of cleanliness in the fillet weld.

NARRATIVE: on december 4, 2024, at 06:57 eastern standard time (est), columbia gas transmission, llc (columbia) monitoring center received a call from the hocking county sheriff's office reporting a gas leak at the crawford storage facility, located on bigham road, rockbridge, ohio, 43149. operations personnel was dispatched and arrived on-site at 07:23 est, where they confirmed the incident. a truck had struck a wellhead lead line, resulting in the breakage of a 1-inch blowoff valve. by 07:50 est, the leak was isolated, and the facility was removed from service. according to a statement from the driver, he was in the area for deer hunting and was using the site to turn around. he had his vehicle's dome light on and did not see the above-ground piping. the event has been reported as an incident due to the estimated cost of damages potentially exceeding $147,400. the well master valve was replaced on the week of april 1, 2025. the replacement lead line has been fabricated and was installed the week of june 10, 2025. the storage team removed bridge plug and put the line back to service on july 26, 2025.

NAME: CNX MIDSTREAM PARTNERS LP
NARRATIVE: on 02/10/2025, a landowner contacted a cnx representative to inquire about an audible potential gas release at the mor40 valve setting. it was initially assumed the observed noise was from contemporaneous cnx pigging operations blowing down the barrel at bailey valve set to launch a pig. the cnx representative contacted the landowner back to relay that information and the landowner thanked the cnx representative for the response. during this pigging operation that was conducted pursuant to cnx pigging procedures and operational parameters, the pressure increased in the 1260 mor40 u2 pipeline (upstream of the pipeline being pigged). based on a trend of the data, the pressure appears to have remained below the maop of the pipeline and the set-point for the prv located upstream at the mor40 well pad. however, the prv opened at this time. the prv remained open and released gas until a production operator arrived onsite approximately two hours later and found the prv relieving. the production operator secured the release within approximately 9 minutes of his finding. the prv was set to relieve at 1300 psig; based on the pressure data trend it appears to have relieved at approximately 1126 psig. the prv was tested on 02/11/2025 and found to relieve at 1148 psig; it was then reset to 1300 psig. the prv was later thoroughly inspected by the manufacturer (mercer) who found evidence of normal wear on valve internal components. the manufacturer stated that this wear could cause a potential leak, which in turn could cause a valve to activate below its set pressure; in addition, the manufacturer tested the spring for proper function and found it to be within tolerance. after completing their inspection, no definitive cause for the sub-set pressure activation was identified by the manufacturer. cnx has taken this valve out of service and replaced it with a new valve to avoid a recurrence.

NAME: TARGA RESOURCES OPERATING LLC
NARRATIVE: a project was initiated to install a pig trap approximately one mile from the irion compressor station. originally delayed due to inclement weather, the pipeline was successfully isolated and vented to a flare on january 29, 2025. a contract inspector working for applied consultants, issued the work permit, authorizing the night contract crew to commence cold-cutting and welding operations within a bell hole. to mitigate the presence of fumes emanating from both ends of the pipeline inside the bell hole, contractors installed plugs to facilitate hot work. a formans plug was placed at the opposite end of the worksite, while a mud plug was positioned behind the area where the welder would be beveling and welding. once the visible gas fumes dissipated from the bell hole, the welder and his assistant entered the space to prepare for beveling. the four-gas monitor was checked to confirm the absence of lower explosive limits (lels) in the area. at approximately 3:00 am, the welder ignited his torch at the end of the pipe to verify the presence of any residual gas. moments later, a flash fire erupted around the welder, igniting his clothing and resulting in burn injuries. the investigation showed that the mud plug located behind the welder was leaking gas fumes into the immediate area. the four-gas monitor used to detect the lels, was sitting at the top of the bell hole with a three-foot hose hanging into the six-foot hole, approximately six to eight feet from the work location. at this distance and location, the monitor was unable to detect the atmosphere in the work area. the cause was determined to be incorrect operation of gas monitoring equipment. targa has initiated multiple efforts to mitigate and prevent recurrence. a mud plug installation procedure has been developed as guidance for contractors working for targa. additionally all contract inspectors have been retrained on safety enforcement expectations and proper use of gas monitoring.

CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: operations discovered gas leak at mp 97.15 on svl-t-t-t with handheld leak survey equipment. after confirmation, line pressure was regulated to 80% of operating pressure and existing pressure was drawn down by a downstream customer. after excavation, a transverse crack was visually identified on the pipe body. the line was subsequently isolated, further drawn down by customers with remaining pressure blown down. the pipe segment was then cut out and replaced with pretested piping. the cutout pipe was sent to a metallurgical lab for analysis. lab analysis concluded the following: the primary failure mechanism was stress corrosion cracking (scc), driven by residual tensile stresses from preexisting bending during construction in combination with a mildly corrosive, oxygen-depleted environment. scc may not have occurred in the absence of pipe bending during construction, highlighting the critical role of mechanical loading in this failure. unintentional loss volume was updated and reduced after further analysis.

NAME: UGI ENERGY SERVICES
NARRATIVE: on march 20, 2025, compressor #2 was placed in maintenance mode for troubleshooting an esd vent valve status issue. loose terminals in the actuator control board were identified and repaired. however, maintenance mode was accidentally left active overnight. the maintenance mode should have triggered local alarms and sms notifications at 2, 12, and 24 hours, but sms alerts failed to generate. operators missed the maintenance status on local scada displays the morning of march 21. at 12:24 on march 21, compressor #2 suction and discharge block valves unexpectedly closed. normally this would trigger unit shutdown, but maintenance mode blocked all shutdown signals, forcing the compressor to run with closed valves until 13:05 when operators received a loss of run status alarm. personnel arrived at 13:14 and assessed damage. during inspection, a small oil fire was detected by the safety system, causing station esd at 13:23. operations personnel immediately extinguished the fire. post-incident scada analysis revealed both valves opened without command after the compressor stopped. the engine control panel indicated shutdown due to mechanical overload. the valve closure caused catastrophic mechanical failure requiring complete replacement of frame, crankcase, crankshaft, cylinders, and associated components. the maintenance mode capability has been eliminated from station plc programming. root cause was identified as malfunction in valve control circuitry, hardware, wiring, and connections between plc and valve actuators. due to the intermittent nature, specific component isolation was impossible during online operation. investigation eliminated plc programming and hardware, narrowing the fault to physical connections including i/o boards, cabinet connections, and field wiring. historical review revealed similar valve closures previously misdiagnosed as pneumatic issues. prior to restart, all plc i/o boards for block valve control were replaced, wiring continuity verified, and actuator terminations inspected. since returning to service april 29, 2025, no unexpected valve position changes occurred. combined with removal of problematic maintenance functions and new maintenance mode safeguards, we are confident the root cause is resolved and similar electrical failures would not result in the same incident type.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on march 25th, 2025, at approximately 09:51 eastern daylight time (edt), the presence of natural gas was identified by tc energy project personnel while performing a casing mitigation project, a subsequent leakage survey was conducted to identify the location of the source of this gas release. on march 26th at approximately 10:00 edt, after further investigation, it was identified the leak was from a valve stem on line d-76 near the ohio state route19 highway. at approximately 13:26 edt it was confirmed the cost of repair may exceed $145,400 and the incident was promptly reported to the national response center (nrc). the initial plan for repair was to install stopples, bypass the valve, the casing and gas pipeline located under the highway. on april 3rd, 2025, at approximately 15:00 edt a mechanical fitting that was located a few feet downstream of the leaking valve failed and caused the release of approximately 7,254 mcf of natural gas into the atmosphere. the project team evacuated the site of the incident and called the emergency responders. ohio sr 19 highway was closed at 15:25 edt, and 129 residences were evacuated. a courtesy call was made to the public utilities commission of ohio chief ' facility and operations field division at 15:27 edt and phmsa accident incident division at 15:39 edt. there was no fire, explosion, injury, or fatality. at 18:49 pm edt the affected section of the pipeline was isolated and blown down. there was a loss of gas service to two columbia gas of ohio points of delivery. the repair was completed by removing the failed mechanical fitting and leaking valve. line d-76 was returned into service on april 6, 2025, at 16:45 edt. the failed mechanical fitting and leaking valve were protected and preserved as evidence and sent to a local tc energy office for further investigation. the root cause failure analysis is complete, and tc energy is actioning the corrective actions.

NAME: PACIFIC GAS & ELECTRIC CO
NARRATIVE: on thursday, march 27, 2025, at approximately 19:30 an unintentional release of gas occurred during a clearance operation. the crew inadvertently unscrewed the isolation ball valve from the active pipeline while attempting to remove the ili antenna that was screwed into it. during the removal of the temporary antenna, the ball valve between the antenna and the pipeline unthreaded from the sav-a-valve (sav), releasing gas into the atmosphere. the crew did not utilize a backup wrench on the isolation ball valve to prevent it from unthreading from the sav. other contributing factors include insufficient procedures and unclear project scope. there were no injuries or fatalities; no media was reported on site. at approximately 21:45, pg&e regulatory compliance personnel determined this to be a dot and cpuc reportable incident meeting the unintentional gas loss exceeding 3,000 mcf.

NAME: ENERGY TRANSFER COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on april 8, 2025, energy transfer (et) personnel detected a fire while on et site near the 97 dehy to coy city pipeline at 14:30. operations began to take precautionary measures and completely isolated the line at 15:15 and the fire was allowed to burn out. et personnel confirmed discovery on april 9th at 10:30 and determined that the incident would exceed the cost reporting threshold. the line has been repaired and was returned to service at 23:47 on april 11th, 2025. the cause of the incident is currently unknown, and the investigation is underway. the lab analysis determined that the rupture was the result of internal corrosion caused by stress-oriented hydrogen induced corrosion (sohic). to prevent this from occurring in the future, the maop of the pipeline will be lowered and the corrosion inhibitor program will be evaluated for effectiveness against h2s corrosion.

NAME: MISSISSIPPI HUB, LLC
CAUSE: MATERIAL FAILURE OF PIPE OR WELD
NARRATIVE: at 20:52 cdt on 4/12/2025, an 8-inch pressure relief valve (prv) attached to a 42-inch header at the mississippi hub ungsf and compressor station was ejected due to a rupture of the pipe spool below the valve. as a result of the event, the on-site operations controller experienced a loss of communications with the scada system. however, the station esd system functioned as designed and shut in the facility automatically. the facility was in the process of preparing to withdraw gas from storage when the event occurred. the on-site operator was joined by other local employees and began investigating the source of the failure when the ejected prv was discovered. the prv was located between the gas heaters and separators downstream of the pressure regulators for the comingled gas stream which was not within the ungsf demarcation. it was determined that the extent of physical damage and corrections to communications could not be fully evaluated until daylight, but there was no concern for the safety of employees or the public. there were no injuries to personnel, ignition of the gas, evacuations, road closures, or media inquiries. the following morning, personnel determined the prv had been ejected vertically and through a cable tray, resulting in multiple damaged cables. once the preliminary extent of the damage had been assessed, it was determined the facility would be shut in while repairs were made. the event was reported to the nrc at 11:09 cdt on 4/13/2025 since repairs could have exceeded $145,400 and we determined at that time that the event resulted in the emergency shutdown of an ungsf. the repair was completed on 4/16/2025, and communications for the facility were restored, allowing the facility to be placed back into service on 4/18/2025. the failed pipe underwent metallurgical examination, and a root cause analysis was undertaken to determine the cause of the failure. the metallurgical analysis determined the pipe spool failure was the result of an external overload of the assembly created by a pressure release event. the pressure release caused a downward force and bending moment, triggering buckling instability just below the pressure relief valve. the components of the assembly above the buckle rotated nearly 45� from vertical before a parting failure occurred. a bulge was progressively generated as the structure bent over, dissipating significant energy. micrographs show that the material exhibited significant plastic flow before failure. the overall plastic behavior of the material local to the bulge was consistent with mechanical testing results. mechanical testing shows an elongation of 32% to 36% and a reduction in area of 66% to 72%. subsize charpy v-notch test specimens (5 mm x 10 mm) returned an average toughness of 98 ft-lbs at 72�f(converted to full scale). the final fracture initiation was caused by shear overload at the buckle bulge tip on the od. no signs of preexisting id or od cracks, damage, corrosion, or other stress risers were found. no evidence existed that prior damage weakened the buckling resistance of the structure. a finite element analysis of the pipe assembly was undertaken to support the conclusion the pipe spool failure was the result of an external overload of the assembly created by a pressure release event. the plastic collapse overload is consistent with the fea engineering analysis results.

NAME: SCOUT ENERGY MANAGEMENT LLC
CAUSE_DETAILS: VALVE LEFT OR PLACED IN WRONG POSITION, BUT NOT RESULTING IN AN OVERPRESSURE
NARRATIVE: 4-28-2025 at 14:30 gas flow on the tema 2001 line was reversed to go to a different third party pipeline. 4-29-25 at 7:01, measurement tech notified operations of a possible leak at uly south. when the scout foreman arrived the foreman found the tema 2001 psv had lifted. foreman closed valve to the psv at approximately 7:52 after checking line pressures. upon investigation, we found that the block valve below the psv had not been blocked in resulting in the psv lift. the psv is used to protect the ubs compressor station from overpressure and is set well below maop of the tema 2001 pipeline. this psv is not needed when gas flow is reversed to go to the third party. the original procedure did not indicate the valve needed to be in the closed position while the offload of gas was being performed. in addition the original procedure has been amended to reflect the valve should be closed during the offload process. although type c gathering lines do not require operator qualifications, we believe this employee has had adequate training to perform this procedure. the employee performing this task has 30+ years of experience in the field operating valves. the employee has also reviewed the amended procedure.

NAME: KEYSPAN ENERGY DELIVERY - NY CITY
NARRATIVE: (see below for updates on supplemental reports) national grid had previously performed an inline inspection of a portion of the 30-inch 350 psig jamaica bay line transmission pipeline in brooklyn, ny, and was preparing to return the pipeline to normal operating status. one of the steps was to insert a completion plug into a 2-inch thread-o-ring (tor) fitting operating at 310 psig. during this process, a failure from an unknown source occurred, resulting in an unplanned, accidental release of natural gas. a company employee was injured and hospitalized as an inpatient; and a second employee was treated at a hospital. the fitting and materials believed to be involved in this incident will be cut out from the 30-inch pipeline and tested by a third-party lab to help determine the apparent cause. *** supplemental report issued 7/24/2025: the 30-inch pipeline was shut down during the weekend of 5/31/2025, and the section in question was removed for further examination and analysis. (cause still unknown). a replacement section was installed, and the 30-inch pipeline was gassed back into service on 6/4/2025. no additional costs are associated with the emergency response. the section was cleaned and then sent to an independent metallurgical laboratory on 6/4/2025. analysis is ongoing. report updated with: entered date/time of restart (section a question 16a and b). latitude/longitude coordinates in a5 reflect the location of the damaged tor and valve assembly. no further change is needed. *** supplemental final report issued 7/15/2026: based on the investigation, the incident involved geometric fitment issues associated with certain t.d. williamson (tdw) 2-inch thread-o-ring (tor) fittings that may have affected plug insertion and thread engagement. engineering analyses, field inspections, and instrumented testing identified additional contributing factors, including undersized tor internal diameters, debris accumulation, and potential swaging. additional investigation identified that the manufacturer's instructions were not properly incorporated into internal work methods, the instructions were not complete and were not fully adhered to during the plug insertion process. the completion plug involved in the incident was not recovered, so failure analysis thereof was not possible. the tor fitting involved in the incident did not exhibit any visible damage whatsoever, including internal threads, but it did exhibit an id too small for plug insertion, possibly due to swaging of the tor or poor quality control by the manufacturer. report updated with: additional facility information (part c) updated with identified material apparent cause (part g) updated from g8 to g7 and details added

NARRATIVE: on may 9, 2025, an incident occurred on the 210000 - perkins 10" hp to ft chadbourne, 6.14 miles southwest of silver, texas in coke county. at approximately 1930 the line had a release. it was determined to be a rupture that occurred during routine maintenance pigging operations. on may 16, 2025, at 1230, it was determined the repairs would exceed the $145,400.00 reportable dollar criteria and the nrc and the txrrc were notified. the line separation is still under investigation and the affected section of the pipe has been sent to the lab for analysis. a supplemental report will be submitted when the lab analysis and investigation is complete. **the lab results concluded that the failure coincides with a region of internal corrosion present along the bottom of the pipe. the internal corrosion occurred due to hydrogen sulfide and carbon dioxide combining with water to form an acidic environment. to prevent this from occurring in the future, operations will implement a pigging schedule and corrosion inhibitor program specific for the pipeline. coupons will be added before the line is put back into service. a supplemental report will be submitted once the pipeline has been put back into service. **on september 19, 2025, at approximately 1000 the line was put back into service.

NAME: HARVEST MIDSTREAM COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on may 19, 2025, harvest initiated a routine foam pigging operation on the pggs system at approximately 11:00 am as part of standard maintenance activities. the pig was launched without incident; however, pressure in the pg-02 segment began to rise unexpectedly later that afternoon. this segment is equipped with a 6-inch pressure relief valve (prv) and emergency shutdown valve (esdv-1), monitored by pressure transmitter pt-201. during the investigation, it was determined that the pig arrived significantly earlier than anticipated. the travel time had been projected using NAME: CRESTWOOD MIDSTREAM PARTNERS LP
NARRATIVE: on may 25, 2025, at 7:57 a.m., while maintenance was being performed by an energy transfer company (etc) employee and a contract employee, the west slash unit 2 compressor, caught fire. the etc employee notified the operations manager who then notified emergency services. the employee and contract employee activated the emergency shut down system (esd) successfully shutting down the compressor station. both the etc employee and contract employee were injured when the fire ignited. when emergency services arrived at the location the two injured received medical attention and the fire was extinguished. the internal investigation found that employees failed to properly follow the lockout/tagout procedure located in s-230 hazardous energy control section xii. the investigation also found that the employees wrongfully opened a valve allowing the natural gas line pressure to purge debris from the cylinders. the released gas then found an ignition source supplied by one or more of the running natural gas compressors resulting in the fire. the plan to prevent recurrence is as follows: 1) safety stand down for the entire wester division to review lockout/tagout procedures and acceptable cleaning media. 2) retrain site employees on s-230 with an emphasis on the proper lockout/tagout process.

NARRATIVE: on june 6th 2025 12:11pm mst clay basin cs unit 1 automatically shutdown due to simultaneous high turbo vibration and engine vibration alarms. approximately 32 seconds later, gas was detected in the building, triggering an emergency shutdown (esd) of the entire station. one field personnel was present in the compressor building, but not in the vicinity of the failure. the unit 1 compressor crosshead shoe separated from the crosshead and was jammed into the crosshead causing the frame to break. the compressor rod was bent as a part of the failure destroying the gas packing causing a gas release to occur. incident investigation is ongoing. preliminary indications points towards contributing factor of a bolt and stud failure that caused the shoe to be loose. action taken during the interim of the investigation was all other units at kastler cs were inspected to ensure all crosshead nuts had not been loosened.

NARRATIVE: on june 15, 2025, an emergency shutdown (esd) event occurred at the washington ranch compressor station while the station was in an idle operating state. severe weather and flash flooding in the area prevented epng personnel from accessing the station until june 16, 2025. during this period, the station was monitored through remote system access which indicated isolation valves and esd vents were in their proper positions. upon arriving on site, epng personnel conducted an onsite assessment and found esd valve 5107 in a partially closed position. a root cause analysis determined that valve 5107 had a defective valve actuator that prevented full valve closure during the esd event and contributed to a release of approximately 84,000 mcf of natural gas. the event was initially classified as an abnormal operation event. subsequent review of measurement data identified that the volume of gas release exceeded reportable thresholds on june 19, 2025, at which time kinder morgan notified the national response center of a reportable natural gas release. corrective action included replacement of the valve actuator on esd valve 5107 to ensure full closure during future esd activations.

NARRATIVE: on june 18, 2025, natural gas vented to the atmosphere through blowdown stacks at tennessee gas pipeline's (tgp) compressor station 856 in savannah, tennessee. the venting occurred when the station's emergency shutdown (esd) system was activated due to a shorted wire associated with the discharge-side valve. the wiring fault caused the control system to indicate that the valve was in the closed position when it was actually open. as a result, the side-gate valves began to open based on the false closed indication from the discharge-side valve. following the incident investigation, the plc cabinet was relocated to a higher elevation to reduce the potential for water intrusion and prevent future wiring-related failures.

NAME: NORTHERN BORDER PIPELINE COMPANY
NARRATIVE: on july 3, 2025, at 16:24 mdt, northern border's gas control (gc) received an alarm at monchy meter station and at 16:36 mdt, gc received a call from a customer about a pressure drop on their compressor station that may have impacted monchy meter station. at 18:38 mdt, a second call was received from the customer asking for a technician on our side to investigate a relief valve at monchy meter station. gc dispatched a technician to investigate a potential release at 18:45 mdt. upon arriving on site at 21:17 mdt, the technician discovered natural gas was being released to the atmosphere through an eight-inch relief valve. immediate action was taken to isolate the valve, which ended the release at 21:20 mdt. the unintentional gas loss was calculated to be approximately 217,850.1 mcf. there were no damages, injuries or hospitalizations. after technicians determined replacement of the pilot valve did not result in reseating, the failed relief valve was removed and sent to a third-party vendor for inspection. the inspection revealed scoring and damage on the main valve piston and piston liner, in addition to deterioration of the main valve seat. the suspected cause of the damage to the valve is accumulation of debris over time, which resulted in the inability of the valve to seal and the unintended release of gas to atmosphere. a secondary relief valve at the monchy meter station is currently providing overpressure protection to the pipeline system.

NAME: EL PASO NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: on july 6th, 2025, the epng plains compressor station went offline following a loss of commercial power, resulting in an increase in system pressure on the epng l1115-l1102 interconnect system. the pressure reached at or near the relief valve's preset limit of 580 psig, causing the relief valve to actuate and vent 17,513 mcf of natural gas into the atmosphere. the kinder morgan gas control team was notified by the sheriff's department operator, and the local operations team were dispatched to the site. the gas control team redirected gas flow upstream of the relief valve to lower the pressure. the relief valve functioned as intended and re-seated once pressure on the line was lowered. the epng plains compressor station was subsequently restored to service without any further issues.

NARRATIVE: at 8:05 a.m., a fasken operator notified oneok pipeline control center of a gas release at the fasken meter setting. upon receiving the report, pcc called the local measurement technician to head to the site. the tech arrived on site at 9:25 a.m and witnessed a prv releasing gas. the tech isolated the prv at 9:27 a.m. after being isolated, the pressure data was trended, and a pressure change was noted to have occurred at 5:51 a.m. the relief for the valve was removed and sent off for analysis. at this time there are no plans to reinstall a new relief as this is a redundant form of pressure control for this setting. once analysis results have been received a supplemental will be submitted. supplemental- following the event, owt conducted a failure analysis. the analysis concluded that the root cause of the failure was the installation of a prv with a relief tolerance within the normal operating range of the pipeline system. this allowed the pvr to continue to relief within the normal design/operating pressure of the pipeline system. as a result, the pvr stem and seats were damaged, not allowing the pvr to reseat. the pvr is a redundant form of pressure control and has been isolated from the system.

NAME: NORTHERN NATURAL GAS CO
NARRATIVE: at 14:05 hours on august 6, 2025, a northern natural gas operations technician discovered a relief valve venting at the minneapolis, minnesota no. 1r (station no. 753160) in carver, minnesota. the operations team contacted the local fire department and sheriffs department to support with the closing of county road 40. the road was successfully closed at 14:24 hours until the operations team was able to divert flow through the station bypass and successfully stopped the relief valve venting at 14:28 hours. the county road was then reopened at 14:35 hours. during the onsite inspection of the relief valve the operations team, it was believed that the relief valve and relief pilot valve were damaged by debris preventing it from reseating and closing. the debris was suspected to have originated from recent nearby construction on the pipeline. when the regulator strainers were examined, they were found to have become dislodged, releasing any debris they held. the relief valve and relief valve pilot were rebuilt on-site and verified for proper operation. at 17:00 hours on august 7, 2025, the station was put back into normal operations. following the incident, the relief valve pilot was sent to the vendor to be examined by a material specialist. the specialist found that the pilot disk had weakened causing the pilot to fail open damaging the relief valve boot due to the high velocity of gas venting through the relief valve. this style of pilot disk was known by specialist to weaken over time, and it is no longer being used by the vendor. northern natural gas is looking at replacing all pilot disks of this style.

NARRATIVE: on august 28, 2025, there was a release of gas at the snapping turtle compressor station located in wind ridge, pa which is owned and operated by eqt production. chief inspector troy leek called the eqt environmental, health, & safety (ehs) hotline to report a gas release at the snapping turtle compressor station. upon arrival to the location, he observed the richhill township fire department (who had been dispatched to the location upon community notification), staged ~150' away on the shared access road. all contract personnel were mustered outside of the gate. the operations supervisor (john mincin) was notified. gas control was contacted to initiate a remote shut in of compressor unit #3, and operations personnel were dispatched to the site. upon examination, there was a tubing failure on a relief valve inside the station. upon evaluation, operations determined that no overpressure event occurred. pressure was ~917psi when the prv lifted. it was noted that the nut and ferrule of the 1/8" stainless steel tubing broke at the pilot which, by design, caused a loss of pressure to the main valve dome thus triggering a fail-open condition (caused the relief valve to lift). the suspected failure is excessive vibration, so new tubing was installed in a configuration that alleviated the vibration issue. eqt production examined other stations with similar tubing configurations as the failed tubing and found them to be fully operational for many years and without vibration issues. eqt production believes that this was an isolated event and particular to the relief valve tubing at this specific relief valve at snapping turtle compressor station.

NAME: COLUMBIA GAS TRANSMISSION, LLC
NARRATIVE: on september 12, 2025, at 13:37 columbia gas transmission, llc (columbia) monitoring center received a call from the maryland emergency service regarding a potential natural gas release from a columbia facility near terra alta, wv. columbia operations personnel responded and were on site at 15:25 and confirmed that the unintended gas release to be from line 8234. the involved section of line 8234 in this event is submerged within the north branch of the potomac river on the md-wv line, and the pipeline resides below the bottom of the riverbed. water levels were low, and current had significantly slowed down, resulting in kayakers seeing an area of water with increased bubbling. garrett county 911 received a call from kayakers about the leak, reporting an odor of gas. pipeline technician arrived on site at 15:25 and found a non-hazardous leak. neither the technician nor firefighters who were at the location saw any dead fish or notable effects on wildlife. the technician reported no sheen on the water. national response center (nrc) was notified of the leak around 16:07 on the day of discovery, and the 48-hour nrc report number was completed on september 14. the nrc 1-hr. report and 48-hr. report numbers were 1442591 and 1442688, respectively. site monitoring has been increased to once a week to ensure the non-hazardous leak conditions do not worsen prior to being permanently replaced. note: all recorded times are in eastern daylight time (edt).

NAME: EASTERN GAS TRANSMISSION AND STORAGE, INC.
NARRATIVE: on 9/12/2025 at approximately 19:32, up-24 ruptured at station 125+05 near the drip and launcher / receiver at the uw-204 well pad in forbes state forest which is located west of farmington, pa in fayette county. gas control received initial indication of the rupture from scada pressure drop alarms on up-2, up-5, and up-7 at 19:32. up-24 is an 8 inch diameter transmission pipeline in storage function approximately 2.3 miles long and transports gas between other transmission pipelines in storage function and uw-204 which is an underground storage well in north summit storage. the maximum allowable operating pressure of up-24 is 3377 psig. up-24 was in normal operation with an operating pressure of 3176 psig and no flow when the incident occurred. at approximately 20:20, operations personnel called gas control and confirmed that natural gas was blowing in north summit storage. fayette county 911 called gas control at approximately 20:31 and provided a similar notification. operations personnel manually closed valve up-24 upstream of up-24 at approximately 20:55 and manually closed the master gate valve and lead lines on uw-204 downstream of up-24 at approximately 21:20 to complete the isolation of up-24. gas control also initiated commands to remotely close valves up-5 and up-116 to support the isolation of up-24 at approximately 20:57. gas ceased blowing from up-24 at approximately 21:29. the rupture resulted in the longitudinal and then circumferential failure of pipe going to the drip; an approximately 25 ft by 30 ft hole in the ground approximately 12 ft to 15 ft deep; approximately 14 ft of pipe folding up and coming out of the ground; approximately 1.5 ft of pipe being ejected approximately 73 ft away from the hole; damage to the drip and associated piping; damage to the launcher / receiver and associated piping; damage to a nearby aboveground brine storage tank at the uw-204 well pad and associated piping; approximately 26,067 mcf gas loss from up-24; approximately 3,092 mcf of gas loss from uw-204; and approximately 0.05 barrels of brine spilled to the ground. the gas did not ignite and there were no fires, injuries, fatalities, or evacuations. initial notification (#1442611) was made to the nrc on 9/12/2025 at 20:45. follow up notification (#1442677) was made to the nrc on 9/13/2025 at 20:50. four pieces of up-24 pipe were cut-out at the rupture and were sent to kiefner & associates for failure analysis. the failure analysis report from kiefner was completed and it was confirmed that internal corrosion was the primary cause. as a precautionary measure, the integrity of the uw-204 wellhead and annular vent were inspected on 9/13/2025 and it was confirmed that uw-204 could be safely returned to service once the remediation actions for up-24 were completed and up-24 was returned to service. the isolation of up-24 remained in effect until the following remediation actions were completed: the section of up-24 containing the rupture was replaced which involved the replacement of approximately 180 ft of 8 inch pipe; the drip and associated piping were replaced; the nearby aboveground brine storage tank and associated piping were repaired; and the soil where the brine spilled was cleaned up. in addition to the remedial actions above, the uw-204 site was reconfigured to allow additional piping to be in-line inspected in the future, improve the functionality of the drip, and additional inspections of north summit storage were performed. the estimated cost of the reconfiguration of the uw-204 site and additional inspections of north summit storage was $2,506,965. the launcher / receiver and associated piping are scheduled to be replaced in 2026 so as to be located closer to uw-204 to allow additional piping to be in-line inspected in the future. up-24 was returned to service on 12/10/2025 at approximately 11:30.
